items.name: Tangent conditions L_v^1 ⊂ Z^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) and L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄)
items.statement: ad ρ̄ is M_{n×n}(k) with the adjoint G_F-action via ρ̄. For v ∈ S, c ↦ (1 + εc)ρ̄ gives Z^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) ≅ Hom_{CNL_{Λ_v}}(R_v^□, k[ε]/(ε²)); L_v^1 is the preimage of Hom_{CNL_{Λ_v}}(R_v, k[ε]/(ε²)); it contains the coboundaries, and L_v is its image in H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄).

items.name: The relative tangent complex C^•_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄), its long exact sequence (6.2.23) and Euler characteristic (6.2.24)
items.statement: C^0_{𝒮,T} = C^0(F_S/F, ad ρ̄); C^1_{𝒮,T} = C^1(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈T} C^0(F_v, ad ρ̄); C^2_{𝒮,T} = C^2(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈T} C^1(F_v, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S∖T} C^1(F_v, ad ρ̄)/L_v^1; C^i_{𝒮,T} = C^i(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S} C^{i−1}(F_v, ad ρ̄) for i ≥ 3; differential (φ, (ψ_v)) ↦ (∂φ, (φ|_{G_{F_v}} − ∂ψ_v)). H^i_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄), h^i_{𝒮,T} its cohomology and dimensions. (6.2.23): 0 → H^0_{𝒮,T} → H^0(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈T} H^0(F_v) → H^1_{𝒮,T} → H^1(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈T} H^1(F_v) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S∖T} H^1(F_v)/L_v → H^2_{𝒮,T} → H^2(F_S/F) → ⊕_{v∈S} H^2(F_v) → ⋯ (coefficients ad ρ̄). Since p > 2, H^i(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) = H^i(F_v, ad ρ̄) = 0 for i ≥ 3, so H^i_{𝒮,T} = 0 for i > 3 and (6.2.24) χ_{𝒮,T}(ad ρ̄) = χ(F_S/F, ad ρ̄) − Σ_{v∈S} χ(F_v, ad ρ̄) − Σ_{v∈S∖T} (dim_k L_v − h^0(F_v, ad ρ̄)).

items.name: Dual Selmer group H^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1))
items.statement: The trace pairing (X, Y) ↦ tr(XY) on ad ρ̄ is perfect and G_F-equivariant, so ad ρ̄(1) is the Tate dual of ad ρ̄. For v ∈ S, L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄(1)) is the exact annihilator of L_v under local Tate duality, and H^1_{𝒮^⊥,T}(ad ρ̄(1)) = ker(H^1(F_S/F, ad ρ̄(1)) → ∏_{v∈S∖T} H^1(F_v, ad ρ̄(1))/L_v^⊥).

items.name: Twisting R_i to determinant ε_l^{−1} after a soluble totally real base change
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 7.1.11: the rank-one system ε_l det r_{i,λ} has Hodge–Tate numbers 0, so det r_{i,λ} = ψ_i ε_l^{−1} for a finite-order ψ_i : G_F → M_i^× unramified outside S_i. The obstruction ∂ψ_i ∈ H^2(G_F, {±1}) = Br_F[2] ↪ ⊕_v Br_{F_v}[2] to a square root is supported on S_i. There is a soluble Galois totally real F_1^+/Q, unramified above 𝓛 and linearly disjoint over Q from the normal closure F_1^avoid of F_0^avoid F̄^{ker(r̄_{E,l_1} × ∏_i r̄_{i,λ_i})}, in which each rational prime below a place v ∈ ∪_i S_i has inertia degree divisible by 2[F_v : Q_{p_v}] [CHT08, Lem. 4.1.2]. Then ψ_i|_{G_{FF_1^+}} = φ_i² with φ_i unramified above 𝓛 after a quadratic twist (Grunwald–Wang, [AT09, Ch. X, Th. 5]), and R'_i := R_i|_{G_{FF_1^+}} ⊗ φ_i^{−1} has det r'_{i,λ} = ε_l^{−1}.

items.name: Profinite completion of an abelian group
items.statement: For abelian A, Ahat=lim over positive n of A/nA, with transition maps for divisibility. For multiplicative groups use A/A^n.

items.name: Completed valuation
items.statement: A DVR valuation v:K*→Z induces v:completed K*→Zhat. Its kernel is the image of completed R*; the split decomposition K*=R*×π^Z gives the proof.

items.name: Continuous cohomology limit and descent comparisons
items.statement: On the existing continuous-cohomology carrier, prove the compact/discrete coefficient comparisons, full Hochschild–Serre and compatible passage to inverse/direct limits used in §§3–6, with the requisite Mittag–Leffler and derived-limit hypotheses. Reuse existing low-degree restriction, corestriction, cup products and Shapiro maps.

items.name: Invariant reduction predicate
items.statement: InvΠ(M) is the canonical coefficient-reduction isomorphism in convention I. Construct its map, and prove M^Π saturated in M; do not define the predicate as equality of dimensions without constructing the map.

items.name: Canonical invariant lattice and quotient reduce exactly
items.statement: Set A∞=Hℓ∞^Π∞ and B∞=Hℓ∞/A∞; A∞ is saturated and B∞ free. Fact 3.1 and Inv identify A∞/ℓ=Aℓ=Hℓ^Πℓ and B∞/ℓ=Bℓ=Hℓ/Aℓ, giving 0→B∞ --ℓ→B∞→Bℓ→0. Keep the canonical reduction diagram and snake connecting map; a dimension count alone does not construct it.

items.name: Continuous H¹ class of a representation extension
items.statement: For an exact sequence0→A→H→B→0 of finite free continuous G-lattices over a complete DVR R, choose the continuous R-linear section149. The cocycle c_s(g)=g*s*g⁻¹−s, valued in Hom_R(B,A), defines an independent class in the existing explicit H1. It vanishes exactly when an equivariant continuous section exists, and its reduction and fraction-field images are the corresponding extension classes. For profinite G,148 transports it to canonical cohomology.

items.name: Scalar structure on the existing explicit H¹ quotient
items.statement: Let R be a commutative topological ring, M a topological R-module and G a topological group acting continuously by R-linear maps. The existing additive H1 carrier143 acquires an R-module structure by r[c]=[g↦r c(g)]. Every continuous R-linear equivariant coefficient map induces an R-linear map.

items.name: Invariant lifting obstruction in continuous H¹
items.statement: For a complete DVR R, uniformizer π, finite free continuous G-lattice M with its π-adic topology, there is a natural exact sequence0→M^G/πM^G→(M/πM)^G→H1(G,M)[π]→0 of R-modules. On an invariant residue class m̄ choose a lift m and send it to [g↦(g·m−m)/π]. This does not require compactness of G.

items.name: Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄) and dual Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄) is the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0ρ̄) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄)/L_{Q,x}, where x runs over all primes of Q and L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad^0ρ̄)^{I_x}) if x ∉ Q, and L_{Q,x} = H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄) if x ∈ Q. H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) denotes the corresponding dual Selmer group, i.e. the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1))/L_{Q,x}^⊥, where L_{Q,x}^⊥ is the annihilator of L_{Q,x} under local Tate duality.

items.name: Local Selmer condition H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) at v|p
items.statement: For v|p, H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) is the subspace 'defined as in Sect. 2.4 of [27]' (DDT). The paper gives no other description. It is the local condition L_{Q,v} at v|p in the Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄). The proof of Proposition 5.1 bounds it via DDT Proposition 2.27 (p split), and via CHT Corollary 2.4.3 with the inclusion H^1(G_{F_p}/I_{F_p}, k) ⊂ H^1_f(F_p, adρ̄) ∩ H^1(F_p, k) (p inert). That it contains the tangent space of the finite flat / ordinary conditions (2)–(3) is implicit in that proof but never stated.

items.name: Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄) and dual Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄) is the kernel of H^1(F, ad⁰ρ̄) → ⊕_x H^1(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄)/L_{Q,x}, where x runs over all primes of F and: L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad⁰ρ̄)^{I_x}) if x ∉ Q ∪ {v|p}; L_{Q,x} = H^1(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄) if x ∈ Q (x ∤ p); L_{Q,v} = H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) if v|p (v ∉ Q). H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) denotes the corresponding dual Selmer group.

items.name: GL(1) example: trivial residual character, Selmer and dual Selmer groups
items.statement: Let F be a number field of signature (r1, r2), p an odd prime and ζ_p ∉ F. Take G = GL(1)/F. Up to twist the only residual representation is the trivial character r̄: G_F → F_p^×. Its minimal deformations are the everywhere unramified ones. Here ad(r̄) = F_p and ad(r̄)(1) = μ_p. Define the Selmer condition L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, F_p) as follows: for finite v (including v | p), L_v is the set of classes unramified on inertia; for v | ∞, L_v = H^1(F_v, F_p) = 0. The Selmer group H^1_L(F, F_p) is the group of global classes lying in L_v at every v, i.e. the everywhere-unramified classes. The dual Selmer group H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) is cut out by the annihilators L*_v = L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, μ_p) under local Tate duality. The invariant for this example is ℓ0 = r1 + r2 − 1.

items.name: Selmer group H^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄)
items.statement: H^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄) := ker( H^1(G_{F,S_Q}, ad^0 r̄) → ⊕_{x∈T} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄) ⊕ ⊕_{x∈Q} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄)/L_x ). That is: unramified outside S_Q, trivial at T, and in L_x at x ∈ Q. Write h^1_{L(Q),T} for its k-dimension. For Q = ∅ it is written H^1_{L,T}.

items.name: Dual Selmer group H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) := ker( H^1(G_{F,S_Q}, ad^0 r̄(1)) → ⊕_{x∈Q} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄(1))/L_x^⊥ ). There is no condition at x ∈ T; the dual of 'trivial' is 'everything'. For Q = ∅ it is written H^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)), and it equals H^1(G_{F,S}, ad^0 r̄(1)).

items.name: Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0 r̄) and dual Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0(r̄(1)))
items.statement: H^1_Q(Q, ad^0(r̄)) is the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0(r̄)) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0(r̄))/L_{Q,x}, where x runs over all primes of Q and the local conditions are as follows. For x ∉ Q ∪ {p}, L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad^0(r̄))^{I_x}). For x ∈ Q, L_{Q,x} is as in local-condition-L-Qx. For x = p, L_{Q,p} = L_p is as in local-condition-L-p. H^1_Q(Q, ad^0(r̄(1))) is the corresponding dual Selmer group: the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0(r̄)(1)) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0(r̄)(1))/L_{Q,x}^⊥, where L_{Q,x}^⊥ is the annihilator of L_{Q,x} under local Tate duality (via the trace pairing ad^0 × ad^0(1) → k(1)).

items.name: The finiteness condition (F) and the p-cohomological dimension
items.statement: A profinite group G satisfies (F) if H^i(G,M) is finite for every finite discrete F_p[G]-module and every i ≥ 0; cd_p(G) := sup{i : H^i(G,M) ≠ 0 for some finite discrete F_p[G]-module M}. For a number field E and a finite set S of places, G_{E,S} satisfies (F) with cd_p = 3; for a local field E_w, G_{E_w} satisfies (F) with cd_p = 2.

items.name: §A.2 (continuous étale cohomology, equivariant sheaves and the functor C ↦ C_L)
items.statement: For a site S and a diagram of rings R_• one has M(S, R_•), C^+(S, R_•) and D^+(S, R_•); the case R_• = W_• : ⋯ → W/p³ → W/p² → W/p gives systems F_• with p^lF_l = 0, with lim← and the exact restrictions (−)_l. Example A.2: L(r)_X := (R lim←(μ^{⊗r}_{p•})_X) ⊗_{Z_p}L computes Jannsen's continuous étale cohomology H^q(X, L(r)) [30], and H^q(S_ét, Rπ_!L(r)_X) its variant with proper support. For a profinite G acting on S one has M_G(S, R_•), H^q_G(S, −), the forgetful map to H^q(S, −) with kernel H^q_G(S, −)_0, and C_L := (R lim← C) ⊗_W L (A.1).

items.name: Everywhere locally trivial cohomology
items.statement: For a number field and a commutative group or continuous Galois module M, Sha^i(k,M)=ker(H^i(k,M)→∏_v H^i(k_v,M)), including real places.

items.name: Everywhere locally trivial arithmetic cohomology
items.statement: For finite Galois module M over number field k, Sha^i(k,M)=ker(H^i(k,M)→∏_v H^i(k_v,M)). In the duality theorem use the stipulated modified real terms; degrees 1 and 2 agree with the relevant Tate groups.

items.name: Pointwise internal Hom for discrete modules
items.statement: For continuous discrete abelian Γ-modules C,A, let Hom_pt(C,A) be the additive homomorphisms C→A with topology induced from A^C (pointwise convergence) and conjugation action (g·u)(c)=g u(g^-1 c). Evaluation Hom_pt(C,A)×C→A is jointly continuous and equivariant, and the conjugation action is jointly continuous.

items.name: Pointwise splitting torsor and its continuous class
items.statement: For an exact sequence 0→A→B→C→0 of continuous discrete abelian Γ-modules admitting an abelian-group section, the sections form a continuous affine Hom_pt(C,A)-torsor. A section s gives the continuous cocycle γ(g)=gsg^-1-s; replacing s by s+u changes γ by d⁰u. Its H¹ class is zero iff there is an equivariant abelian-group section.

items.name: Finite-coefficient Laurent residue and cup compatibility
items.statement: For m invertible in F and i,j>0, construct ∂_t:H^i(F((t)),μ_m^⊗j)→H^(i-1)(F,μ_m^⊗(j-1)). It sends the Kummer class of t to1 and satisfies ∂((t) cup inf b)=b with the indicated twists. Inflation and residue form the split short exact sequence of Gille–Szamuely Corollary6.8.8.

items.name: Unbalanced cochain product
items.statement: For a continuous surjection from a compact group Delta to a finite group Theta, a discrete continuous Delta-module A and a Theta-module B, contract a degree-i homogeneous cochain whose last jprime variables factor through Theta against a degree-minus-j Tate cochain of B. For i≥jprime≥j>0 the result has degree i-j and its last jprime-j variables factor through Theta. Finite Delta is included; define the boundary subspaces i=j and j=0 explicitly.

items.name: The shift-difference presentation of lim and lim¹
items.statement: For a countable inverse sequence of abelian groups B_n with f_n:B_(n+1)→B_n, define Δ:∏B_n→∏B_n by Δ(x)_n=x_n−f_n(x_(n+1)). Identify lim B_n with ker Δ and lim¹ B_n with coker Δ as ordinary abelian groups. Short exact sequences of towers give the natural six-term kernel/cokernel exact sequence. For this index category these agree with the zeroth and first derived limit functors, and higher derived limits vanish.

items.name: Profinite topology on the existing factor-set extension
items.statement: Let G be a profinite group and A a profinite abelian group with jointly continuous G-action. For a continuous normalized factor set c:G×G→A, put the product topology on the existing L31 extension E_c. This is a profinite topological group and 1→A→E_c→G→1 is a continuous extension with closed embedded kernel and the quotient topology. The canonical section is continuous.

items.name: Normalized trace complement
items.statement: For k∞=∪k_m and K its completion, extend normalized traces to bounded projections R_m:K→k_m and put X_m=ker R_m, so K=k_m⊕X_m. Tensor with the finite affinoid modules using the specified Banach topology.

items.name: The exponent-two extension F(S)
items.statement: For a totally real number field F and a finite set S of finite places, F(S) is the maximal abelian extension of exponent two unramified at all finite places outside S. No unramified-at-infinity condition is imposed. The paper uses its splitting fields together with, not in place of, the ray class field of modulus (8) times all real places.

items.name: The coadjoint representation and the Selmer group
items.statement: Ad^*: G^dual -> GL(g-tilde) is the coadjoint representation on the Z-dual g-tilde of Lie(G^dual) (Section 8.1). For a Gal(Q_S/Q)-module M, H^1(Z[1/S], M) is its etale (Galois) cohomology and H^1_f(Z[1/S], M) the classes whose restriction to Q_p lies in the Fontaine-Laffaille subgroup H^1_f(Q_p, M) (Hodge weights in [-(p-3)/2, (p-3)/2]); under the paper's assumptions it equals the Bloch-Kato H^1_f(Q, M) (Section 8.3). V := Hom_{Z_p}(H^1_f(Z[1/S], Ad^* rho(1)), Z_p) (122).

items.name: Group cohomology and cup products
items.statement: For a group Γ and a Γ-module M, H^*(Γ, M) is the cohomology of the inhomogeneous cochain complex, with cup products; the classes α ∈ H^*(K_v ∩ Ad(g)K_v, S) appearing in the double-coset model of the derived Hecke algebra and the class ⟨α⟩ of Lemma 2.10 live in such groups.

items.name: Admissible Γ-groups, level-𝒞 completions and the space 𝒫
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). G is admissible if it is topologically generated by {g^{−1}γ(g) : g ∈ G, γ ∈ Γ} and has order (supernatural) prime to |Γ|. For a set 𝒞 of finite Γ-groups, 𝒞̄ is its closure under finite products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients, and G^𝒞 = lim G/M over closed normal Γ-subgroups with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄ (a functor to level-𝒞 groups preserving surjections). 𝒫 is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible |Γ|′-Γ-groups with all G^𝒞 finite, topologized by the basic opens U_{𝒞,H} = {X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}. A finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-group is admissible iff H^Γ = 1 (§7.1).

items.name: Definition 2.3: Property E
items.statement: For a full subcategory C of Γ-groups, H ∈ C has Property E if for every non-split central extension 1 → Z/pZ → G̃ → G → 1 in C (p prime, trivial Γ-action on Z/pZ), every Γ-surjection H → G lifts to a Γ-surjection H → G̃.

items.name: The free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n and Lemma 3.1
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). F_n(Γ) is the free pro-|Γ|′ group on {x_{i,γ} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ} with σ(x_{i,γ}) = x_{i,σγ}; 𝓕_n(Γ) is the closed Γ-subgroup generated by x_i^{−1}γ_j(x_i), x_i = x_{i,1}. Lemma 3.1: 𝓕_n is admissible, and there is a Γ-quotient map π : F_n → 𝓕_n with π ∘ (inclusion) = id. Remark 3.2: as a pro-|Γ|′ group 𝓕_n is free on {x_i^{−1}σ(x_i) : σ ≠ 1}; it is Γ-generated by n elements; and any H Γ-generated by elements h_i^{−1}γ(h_i) is a quotient of 𝓕_n.

items.name: Definition 3.15: the random groups X_{Γ,n,u} and the measures μ_{u,n}, μ_u
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and u > −n, X_{Γ,n,u} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] with S a multiset of n+u independent Haar-random elements of 𝓕_n (u = 1 by default); μ_{n,u}(A) = Prob(X_{u,n} ∈ A) on Borel subsets of 𝒫, and μ_u(A) = lim_n μ_{n,u}(A) on the algebra generated by the basic opens (3.16). For finite 𝒞, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is finite.

items.name: The fundamental short exact sequence and the multiplicities m(𝒞, n, H, G)
items.statement: For finite 𝒞, a Γ-surjection ϖ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H with kernel N, and M the intersection of the maximal proper (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroups of N: 1 → R → F → H → 1 with F = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/M, R = N/M (4.1), induced by 1 → R → F⋊Γ → H⋊Γ → 1 (4.2); R is a product of irreducible F⋊Γ-groups. 𝒜_H is the set of non-trivial finite abelian irreducible |Γ|′-(H⋊Γ)-groups and 𝒩 the set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups isomorphic to T^j (T non-abelian simple); m(𝒞, n, H, G) is the multiplicity of G in R (summed over the compatible F⋊Γ-structures for G ∈ 𝒩), independent of ϖ (Remark 4.9).

items.name: Definition 5.1, Lemma 5.2 and Corollary 5.3: Γ-chief factor pairs
items.statement: For a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group G, CF_Γ(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of chief factor pairs (M, A) ∈ CF(G⋊Γ) with gcd(|M|, |Γ|) = 1, and CF_Γ(𝒞) = ∪_{G∈𝒞} CF_Γ(G). Lemma 5.2: if 𝒞 is closed under Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients then CF_Γ(𝒞̄) = CF_Γ(𝒞). Corollary 5.3: if all groups in 𝒞 have order ≤ ℓ, then for (M, A) ∈ CF_Γ(𝒞̄) the prime-to-|Γ| part of |A/Inn(M)| is < ℓ, and CF_Γ(𝒞̄) is finite.

items.name: Monic fixed-degree polynomial family
items.statement: M(n)={A∈ℤ[T]: A monic, deg A=n}, with n∈ℕ; M_p(n) is the analogous family over 𝔽_p for prime p. M(0)={1}.

items.name: Independent coefficient product law
items.statement: For probability masses μ_0,…,μ_{n−1} on ℤ, PM(n)(A)=∏_{j<n}μ_j(coeff_j A) on M(n). Independence is across coefficient positions, not across reductions at different primes; identical distribution is not assumed.

items.name: Uniform nonzero-constant coefficient family
items.statement: For finite N⊂ℤ with |N|≥2 and n≥1, Υ_N(n) consists of monic degree-n polynomials whose n nonleading coefficients lie in N and whose constant coefficient is nonzero; equip it with uniform probability. Its cardinality is |N\{0}|·|N|^(n−1).

items.name: Joint reduction at several primes
items.statement: For a finite set ℙ of distinct primes, P=∏p∈ℙ p. Reduce a single A∼PM(n) coefficientwise to A_ℙ=(A mod p)_p in ∏M_p(n); its law is the pushforward of PM(n). It need not equal a product of its marginals.

items.name: Vector polynomial ring, divisibility and norm
items.statement: For finite ℙ, 𝔽_ℙ[T]=∏_{p∈ℙ}𝔽_p[T]. For a tuple D of monic polynomials, ||D||_ℙ=∏p p^(deg D_p); divisibility, gcd, lcm and congruence are coordinatewise. M_ℙ(ℓ)=∏M_p(ℓ_p).

items.name: Coset Fourier control
items.statement: For P>1 squarefree, s>0 and real γ, α(s,γ;P)=max_{QR=P,Q>1,ℓ mod R} Q^(γ−1)Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s. Write α(P)=α(1,1/2;P).

items.name: Fourier product σ
items.statement: For X∈∏𝔽_p((1/T)), σ_ℙ(n;X)=∏_{j=0}^{n−1}|μhat_j(ψ_ℙ(T^jX))|, where ψ is item 13. This is the modulus of the characteristic function of the random polynomial pairing.

items.name: Joint congruence discrepancy Δ
items.statement: For real m≥0, Δ_ℙ(n;m)=Σ_{D_p monic,deg D_p≤m,T∤D_p ∀p} max_{C mod D}|P(A_ℙ≡C mod D)−1/||D||_ℙ|. All maxima and sums are finite; m is truncated by integer degrees.

items.name: Reduced-fraction discrepancy δ
items.statement: For ℓ_p≥0 integers, δ_ℙ(n;ℓ)=(∏p p^(ℓ_p))^(-1)Σ_{H∈M_ℙ(ℓ),T∤H_p}Σ_{G mod H,(G_p,H_p)=1 ∀p}σ_ℙ(n;G/H).

items.name: Nonconstant divisor event
items.statement: For monic A of degree n and real b, Bad_b(A) means ∃monic D∈ℤ[T], D|A and 1≤deg D≤b. Unit divisors are excluded. For n≥2, A reducible over ℚ iff Bad_{n/2}(A), by Gauss's lemma and factor-degree additivity.

items.name: Polynomial divisor and prime-factor counts
items.statement: For nonzero A∈𝔽_p[T], τ(A) is the number of monic divisors and ω(A) the number of distinct monic irreducible factors. If A=unit·∏I^ν_I, then τ(A)=∏(ν_I+1), ω(A)=#{I:ν_I>0}, and τ(A)≥2^ω(A), with equality for squarefree A.

items.name: Smooth and rough parts excluding T
items.statement: For monic A∈𝔽_p[T] and integer m≥0, A^S(m) is the full product of powers of irreducible factors I≠T with deg I≤m; A^R(m)=A/A^S(m). Thus all powers of T belong to the rough part even when m≥1.

items.name: Additive polynomial functions
items.statement: An additive function f on nonzero 𝔽_p[T] satisfies f(AB)=f(A)+f(B) when gcd(A,B)=1. In Lemma 9.2 it is nonnegative, f(I)∈{0,1} and 0≤f(I^ν)≤C1 log ν for ν≥2,C1≥3.

items.name: Additive-function intensity
items.statement: For f as in item 79 and m≥1, L_f(m)=Σ_{I monic irreducible,deg I≤m,f(I)=1}1/||I||_p. This sum includes T, although A^S(m) excludes T; the difference in the estimates is uniformly bounded.

items.name: Induced partition law
items.statement: For A∼PM(n) and prime p, ν is the pushforward measure on partitions of n under A↦τ_{A_p}. Thus ν(E)=P(τ_{A_p}∈E); it is not assumed to be the partition law of a uniform permutation.

items.name: Optimal Fourier exponents
items.statement: For finitely many coefficient laws, squarefree P>1 and s≥1, define γ(s)∈[0,1] uniquely by max_{j,QR=P,Q>1,0≤ℓ<R} Q^(γ(s)−1) Σ_{k=0}^{Q−1}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s=1. Set θ(s)=γ(s)/s. Include every coefficient index used by the intended criterion.

items.name: Four-prime summability threshold
items.statement: λ0=1/(4−4log2)∈(0.8,0.82). It is characterized by 4(1−log 2)λ0=1 and measures the degree surplus needed to sum the four simultaneous divisor probabilities.

items.name: [n] and coordinate projections
items.statement: For n ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, [n] := {1, …, n}. For a product X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, π_i : X → X_i is the i-th projection. ⊆ denotes inclusion and ⊂ strict inclusion.

items.name: Cubes Cube(X, S), projections π_T, pr_1, pr_2
items.statement: For X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r and S ⊆ [r], Cube(X, S) := ∏_{i∈S} X_i² × ∏_{i∈[r]−S} X_i. For T ⊆ [r], π_T is the projection Cube(X, S) → ∏_{i∈T∩S} X_i² × ∏_{i∈T∩([r]−S)} X_i. pr_1, pr_2 : X_i² → X_i are the two projections.

items.name: Faces x̄(T) of a cube point
items.statement: Let X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, S ⊆ [r], x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) and T ⊆ S. Then x̄(T) is the set of ȳ ∈ Cube(X, T) with π_i(ȳ) ∈ {pr_1(π_i(x̄)), pr_2(π_i(x̄))} for all i ∈ S − T and π_{[r]−(S−T)}(x̄) = π_{[r]−(S−T)}(ȳ).

items.name: N(φ) and the field of definition L(φ)
items.statement: For a profinite group G, a discrete space X and a continuous map φ : G → X, N(φ) is the largest open normal subgroup of G through which φ factors (it exists: at least one exists by continuity, and the subgroups through which φ factors are closed under products). When G is a Galois group, L(φ) is the fixed field of N(φ), the field of definition of φ.

items.name: Up_{K/ℚ}(p) and Up_{K/ℚ}(a)
items.statement: For a prime p ramified in a quadratic field K/ℚ, Up_{K/ℚ}(p) is the unique place of K above p. For a positive squarefree integer a all of whose prime factors ramify in K/ℚ, Up_{K/ℚ}(a) is the unique integral ideal of K of norm a.

items.name: Fixed separable closures and decomposition embeddings
items.statement: Fix a separable closure ℚ^sep of ℚ and, for each place v of ℚ, a separable closure ℚ_v^sep of ℚ_v and an embedding i_v : ℚ^sep → ℚ_v^sep. Restriction along i_v gives a continuous injective homomorphism i_v^* : G_{ℚ_v} → G_ℚ. All number fields are taken inside ℚ^sep.

items.name: Fixed inertia generators σ_v, σ_2(1), σ_2(2)
items.statement: For each v ∈ 𝒫 fix a topological generator σ_v of I_v(2) ≅ ℤ₂. Put I_2(2) := π_{pro-2}(i_2^*(I_2)) and fix σ_2(1), σ_2(2) ∈ I_2(2) with χ_{−1}(σ_2(1)) = 1, χ_{−1}(σ_2(2)) = 0, χ_2(σ_2(1)) = 0 and χ_2(σ_2(2)) = 1. These exist because ℚ(ζ_8)/ℚ is totally ramified at (2).

items.name: Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ), N = ℚ₂/ℤ₂ and the twisted modules N(χ)
items.statement: Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) := Hom_cont(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂) is the set of quadratic characters of ℚ. N := ℚ₂/ℤ₂, with the discrete topology and trivial G_ℚ-action. For χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ), N(χ) is the discrete G_ℚ-module N with σ ·_χ n := (−1)^{χ(σ)} n.

items.name: Definition 2.4 (semidirect-product convention)
items.statement: In N ⋊ 𝔽₂ and N[2^s] ⋊ 𝔽₂ (s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}), the nontrivial element of 𝔽₂ acts on N by −id; so these are generalized dihedral groups.

items.name: Unramified cocycles Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Cocy(G_ℚ, N(χ)), the image of ψ is finite and ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}} ∈ (G_{ℚ(χ)}^{ab})^∨[2^∞]. Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ)) is the preimage of Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨[2^∞] under ψ ↦ ψ|_{G_{ℚ(χ)}}. Here Cl(ℚ(χ))^∨ is identified, via Artin reciprocity for the narrow class group, with the characters of G_{ℚ(χ)} unramified at all finite places.

items.name: Definition 2.8 (raw cocycle)
items.statement: Let χ ∈ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be non-trivial and s ∈ ℤ_{≥0}. A raw cocycle (for N(χ)) is a sequence (ψ_i)_{0≤i≤s} with ψ_i ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[2^i] and 2·ψ_{i+1} = ψ_i for 0 ≤ i ≤ s − 1. Equivalently it is a single ψ_s ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ)) with 2^s ψ_s = 0, with ψ_i := 2^{s−i}ψ_s. By convention ψ_j := 0 for j < 0.

items.name: The cube C, the cochains χ_H and the faces C_T
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{>0}, let (p_i(1), p_i(2))_{i∈[s]} be 2s distinct primes coprime to the squarefree integer d_0, and C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_s(1), p_s(2)} × {d_0}. A point x ∈ C is identified with the squarefree integer d_0 ∏_{i∈[s]} π_i(x). For a finite set H of squarefree integers, χ_H : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂ is σ ↦ ∏_{x∈H} χ_x(σ), a product in 𝔽₂ also used as a {0, 1}-valued indicator. For T ⊆ [s], C_T := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(2) for all i ∈ T}.

items.name: Remark 2.10 (sums of cocycles live in Map_cont(G_ℚ, N))
items.statement: Sums ∑_{x∈C} ψ_j(x) of cocycles for different twists N(x) are taken in the ambient group Map_cont(G_ℚ, N) of continuous cochains, where they are generally not cocycles for any single N(x).

items.name: Definition 2.12 (expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0)
items.statement: Let X ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) be a finite linearly independent set and χ_0 ∈ X. Write 𝔽₂^Y for the free 𝔽₂-vector space on a set Y, and let 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} act on the group ring 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] by translation. An expansion map with support X and pointer χ_0 is a continuous homomorphism ψ : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] ⋊ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} with two properties. First, π_χ ∘ ψ = χ for every χ ∈ X − {χ_0}, where π_χ is the χ-coordinate of 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}. Second, π ∘ ψ = χ_0, where π is the unique nontrivial character vanishing on {0} ⋊ 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}} (the augmentation of the group ring).

items.name: t-coordinates φ_Y(ψ) and the reconstruction formula (2.2)
items.statement: Sending t_x ↦ e_0 + e_x (x ∈ X − {χ_0}, where e_0 is the identity of 𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}) gives 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^{X−{χ_0}}] ≅ 𝔽₂[t_x : x ∈ X − {χ_0}]/(t_x² : x ∈ X − {χ_0}). This ring has 𝔽₂-basis the squarefree monomials t_Y := ∏_{y∈Y} t_y, Y ⊆ X − {χ_0}. The t_Y-coordinate of ψ is a continuous cochain φ_Y(ψ) : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂, and ψ(g) = (∑_{Y⊆X−{χ_0}} φ_Y(ψ)(g) t_Y, (χ(g))_{χ∈X−{χ_0}}) (2.2).

items.name: Normalized expansion maps φ_{S;d}(𝔊)
items.statement: If ψ(𝔊) exists, φ_{S;d}(𝔊) := φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ(𝔊)), where S is the set of squarefree integers corresponding to X − {χ_0} and d is the squarefree integer corresponding to χ_0. Thus for s ≥ 0, a set S of s squarefree integers and a squarefree a_{s+1} with S ∪ {a_{s+1}} spanning an (s+1)-dimensional subspace of ℚ^*/ℚ^{*2}, there is at most one such cochain φ_{S;a_{s+1}}(𝔊). One says that φ_{S;a_{s+1}}(𝔊) exists when there is one. These cochains are the normalized expansion maps.

items.name: The field M(ψ) below the centre
items.statement: For an expansion map ψ with support X (|X| ≥ 2) and pointer χ_0, M(ψ) := ℚ(X) · ∏_{Y⊊X−{χ_0}} L(φ_Y(ψ)), also written M(φ_{X−{χ_0}}(ψ)).

items.name: The degenerate expansion map φ_{a;a}(𝔊) for a ∈ 𝒟
items.statement: Let a ∈ 𝒟. Then χ_a ∪ χ_a = 0 in H²(G_ℚ, 𝔽₂), and there is a unique map φ_{a;a}(𝔊) : G_ℚ → 𝔽₂ with (dφ_{a;a}(𝔊))(σ, τ) = χ_a(σ)·χ_a(τ) that vanishes on every element of 𝔊.

items.name: The Artin pairing ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} of a finite abelian 2-group
items.statement: Let A be a finite abelian 2-group, s ∈ ℤ_{≥1} and A^∨ := Hom(A, ℚ₂/ℤ₂). Define ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(A)} : 2^{s−1}·A[2^s] × 2^{s−1}·A^∨[2^s] → 𝔽₂ by ⟨a, χ⟩ := ψ(a) for any ψ ∈ A^∨ with 2^{s−1}ψ = χ. The value does not depend on the choice of ψ, and it lies in 𝔽₂ = (½ℤ)/ℤ because a ∈ A[2].

items.name: Art_s(x) for a quadratic field and its Galois interpretation
items.statement: For squarefree x ≠ 1, ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(x)} := ⟨−, −⟩_{Art_s(Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^∞])}, with Cl the narrow class group. Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^∞] is identified with the maximal 2-quotient of Cl(ℚ(√x)), and by the Artin map with Gal(H_{2^∞}(ℚ(√x))/ℚ(√x)). Here H_{2^∞}(K) is the largest abelian 2-power extension of K unramified at all finite places. So ⟨b, χ⟩_{Art_s(x)} is the Artin symbol of the 2-torsion class b in a cyclic degree-2^s extension of ℚ(√x), unramified at finite places, whose character ψ satisfies 2^{s−1}ψ = χ.

items.name: Standing setup for higher Rédei reciprocity
items.statement: Let n ∈ ℤ_{≥1}, A ⊆ Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) with |A| = n, and χ_1 ≠ χ_2 in Γ_{𝔽₂}(ℚ) − A. Put A_1 := A ∪ {χ_1} and A_2 := A ∪ {χ_2}. For finite Galois L/ℚ, Ram(L/ℚ) is the set of places of ℚ that ramify in L. Assume: the n sets Ram(ℚ(χ)/ℚ), χ ∈ A, are non-empty, pairwise disjoint and do not contain ∞, so ℚ(A) is totally real and A is linearly independent; and Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) and Ram(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ) are non-empty and disjoint from ⋃_{χ∈A} Ram(ℚ(χ)/ℚ), so each χ_i is independent of A.

items.name: The 4-tuple (A_1, A_2, ψ_1, ψ_2) and its cochains φ_{i,B}
items.statement: ψ_1, ψ_2 : G_ℚ ↠ 𝔽₂[𝔽₂^A] ⋊ 𝔽₂^A are expansion maps with supports A_1, A_2 and pointers χ_1, χ_2. Put φ_{i,B} := φ_B(ψ_i) for B ⊆ A, so that φ_{i,∅} = χ_i. By Proposition 2.14, L(ψ_i)/M(ψ_i) is a central 𝔽₂-extension (i = 1, 2).

items.name: Coprimality constraints on the pointers
items.statement: The pointers χ_1, χ_2 satisfy the coprimality constraints if: (i) Ram(ℚ(χ_1)/ℚ) ∩ Ram(ℚ(χ_2)/ℚ) ⊆ {(2)}; (ii) inv_2(χ_1 ∪ χ_2) = 0, i.e. the local Hilbert symbol of χ_1, χ_2 at 2 is trivial; (iii) χ_1(σ_2(2)) = 0 or χ_2(σ_2(2)) = 0; (iv) (2) splits completely in ℚ(A)/ℚ.

items.name: Definition 3.1 (Rédei admissible 4-tuple; pointer vector; base set)
items.statement: A 4-tuple (A_1, A_2, ψ_1, ψ_2) as above (standing setup and coprimality constraints) is Rédei admissible if four conditions hold. (1) If ∞ splits completely in ℚ(A_1 ∪ A_2)/ℚ, then ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_1)M(ψ_2)/ℚ. (2) Whenever {i, j} = {1, 2} and ∞ ramifies in L(ψ_i)/ℚ, ∞ splits completely in M(ψ_j)/ℚ. (3) Whenever {i, j} = {1, 2} and a place w of ℚ(A) above v ∈ 𝒫 ramifies in L(ψ_i)/ℚ(A), v splits completely in M(ψ_j)/ℚ and v is unramified in L(ψ_j)/ℚ. (4) If L(ψ_1)L(ψ_2)/ℚ is ramified at (2), there are i, j with {i, j} = {1, 2} such that: ψ_i is a normalized expansion map with χ_i(σ_2(2)) = 0 and φ_T(ψ_i) ∘ i_2^* = 0 for every ∅ ≠ T ⊊ A; and χ_i ∘ i_2^* is orthogonal to φ_{T'}(ψ_j) ∘ i_2^* under the local Hilbert pairing at (2) for every T' ⊆ A. (χ_1, χ_2) is the pointer vector and A the base set.

items.name: Reduced ramification set R̃am
items.statement: For a quadratic field ℚ(√d)/ℚ with d squarefree: R̃am(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) := Ram(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) − {(2)} if d has even 2-adic valuation, and R̃am(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) := Ram(ℚ(√d)/ℚ) otherwise. Equivalently, a finite v lies in R̃am iff v(d) is odd, and ∞ lies in R̃am iff d < 0.

items.name: Kummer classes α_{i,B}
items.statement: For i ∈ {1, 2} and B ⊆ A, φ_{i,B}|_{G_{ℚ(B)}} is a quadratic character (by (2.3)), and α_{i,B} ∈ ℚ(B)^*/ℚ(B)^{*2} is its Kummer class; α_{i,∅} = d_i with χ_i = χ_{d_i}. Moreover φ_{i,A}|_{G_{ℚ(A)}} generates a free 𝔽₂[Gal(ℚ(A)/ℚ)]-module of rank 1 whose field is L(ψ_i). So L(ψ_i) is the Galois closure over ℚ of ℚ(A)(√α_{i,A}), and L(ψ_i) = M(ψ_i)(√α_{i,A}).

items.name: w(α) at real places
items.statement: For a real place w of a number field L, given by σ : L → ℝ, and α ∈ L^*: w(α) := 0 if σ(α) > 0, and 1 otherwise. At finite w, w(α) is the valuation.

items.name: Profitable-triple cube C, base point x₀ and sub-cubes C_{p_i(h)}, C_T
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1}; let p_1(1), p_1(2), …, p_s(1), p_s(2) be 2s distinct positive odd primes with p_i(1)p_i(2) ≡ 1 mod 8 for each i ∈ [s]; let d₀ be a positive squarefree integer coprime to ∏_{i∈[s]} p_i(1)p_i(2). Put C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_s(1), p_s(2)} × {d₀}, identifying ((p_i(f(i)))_{i∈[s]}, d₀) (f: [s] → [2]) with the squarefree integer d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s} p_i(f(i)), and x₀ := d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s} p_i(1). For i ∈ [s], h ∈ [2]: C_{p_i(h)} := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(h)}; for T ⊆ [s] and f: T → {1,2}: C_{(p_i(f(i)))_{i∈T}} := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(f(i)) ∀ i ∈ T}; C_T := {x ∈ C : π_i(x) = p_i(2) for all i ∈ T}.

items.name: Triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) (equation (4.1))
items.statement: With C, x₀ as in the §4 setup, let a be a divisor of d₀. A triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) consists of, for each x ∈ C − {x₀}, a raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x) for N(x) (so ψ_{s+1}(x) ∈ Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ_x)), 2^{s+1}ψ_{s+1}(x) = 0, and ψ_j(x) := 2^{s+1−j}ψ_{s+1}(x), ψ_j := 0 for j ≤ 0) satisfying (4.1): ψ_1(x) = 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_a.

items.name: Definition 4.2 (profitable triple)
items.statement: A triple (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) is profitable if for each i ∈ [s]: (1) (∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s+1−|T|}(x))(σ_{p_i(2)}) = 0 for every T ⊆ [s] with i ∈ T; (2) ∑_{x∈C_{p_i(2)}} ψ_{s−1}(x) = 0 (equation (4.2)); (3) the normalized expansion map φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊) exists; (4) every prime l | d₀ splits completely in L(φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ; (5) (2) and ∞ split completely in M(φ_{{p_j(1)p_j(2) : j∈[s]−{i}}; p_i(1)p_i(2)}(𝔊))/ℚ.

items.name: The cochains ψ_T(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}})
items.statement: For a profitable triple and ∅ ⊆ T ⊊ [s], ψ_T(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) := ∑_{x∈C_{[s]−T}} ψ_{|T|+1}(x) ∈ Map_cont(G_ℚ, N). The same formula defines ψ_{[s]} = ∑_{x∈C} ψ_{s+1}(x) once a raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) is also given.

items.name: Attached raw cocycle and attached expansion map of a profitable triple
items.statement: The raw cocycle ψ_{s+1}(x₀) and the expansion map ψ(C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) produced by Theorem 4.6 are called the raw cocycle and the expansion map attached to the profitable triple.

items.name: Special integers and special cubes
items.statement: A squarefree integer d > 1 is special if it has no prime divisor ≡ 3 mod 4. A cube C (as in §4) is special if all its elements are special.

items.name: Definition 5.1 (−1-profitable triple)
items.statement: Let (C, χ_a, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}) be a special profitable triple. It is −1-profitable if (1) φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊) exists; (2) every odd prime divisor of d₀ splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ; (3) (√x) ∈ 2^s·Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^{s+1}] for each x ∈ C; (4) the place (1+i) of ℚ(i) splits completely in M(φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]}; −1}(𝔊))/ℚ(i). Here M(φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊)) = ℚ({χ_{a_i} : i ∈ [s]})·∏_{T⊊[s]} L(φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}}(𝔊)).

items.name: Ramification index e_p(F/ℚ) and residue degree f_p(F/ℚ)
items.statement: For a finite Galois F/ℚ and a prime p, e_p(F/ℚ) := #(proj(G_ℚ → Gal(F/ℚ))∘i_p^*)(I_p) and f_p(F/ℚ) := #(proj(G_ℚ → Gal(F/ℚ))∘i_p^*)(G_{ℚ_p}) / e_p(F/ℚ).

items.name: Definition 5.4 (Pellian expansion map)
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1} and let a_1, …, a_{s+1} be pairwise coprime special squarefree integers > 1. An expansion map (φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}})_{T⊆[s]} with support {a_1, …, a_{s+1}} and pointer a_{s+1} is Pellian if, writing φ := φ_{{a_i : i∈[s]}; a_{s+1}}: (1) for each finite prime p ramified in L(φ)/ℚ, e_p(L(φ)/ℚ) = e_p(M(φ)/ℚ) = 2 and p ≢ 3 mod 4; (2) f_p(M(φ)/ℚ) = 1 for each finite prime p ramified in M(φ)/ℚ; (3) χ_{a_i} is locally trivial at 2 for all i ∈ [s]; (4) ∞ splits completely in M(φ)/ℚ; (5) φ_{{a_i : i∈T}; a_{s+1}}(σ₂(1)) = 0 for each T ⊊ [s]; (6) for each i ∈ [s], all prime divisors of a_i are unramified in L(φ_{{a_j : j∈[s]−{i}}; a_{s+1}})/ℚ.

items.name: Standard-reflection setup: cube with s+1 coordinates; triples of type 1 and type 2
items.statement: Let s ∈ ℤ_{≥1}, C := {p_1(1), p_1(2)} × ⋯ × {p_{s+1}(1), p_{s+1}(2)} × {d₀} with 2s+2 distinct primes coprime to the positive squarefree d₀, such that p_i(1)p_i(2) ≡ 1 mod 8 and p_i(1)p_i(2) is a square modulo every odd prime factor of d₀ for every i ∈ [s] (the proofs use this for every i ∈ [s+1]); a | d₀; x₀ := d₀·∏_{i=1}^{s+1} p_i(1); points identified with squarefree integers. For each x ∈ C − {x₀} let ψ_{s+1}(x) be a raw cocycle for N(x). The triple (C, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}, χ_a) is of type 1 if 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_a for all x ∈ C − {x₀}, and of type 2 if 2^s·ψ_{s+1}(x) = χ_{π_{s+1}(x)·a} for all x ∈ C − {x₀}.

items.name: Definition 5.8 (minimal triple)
items.statement: A triple (C, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}, χ_a) of type 1 is minimal if ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s−|T|+1}(x) = 0 for every nonempty T ⊆ [s+1] (equation (5.3)).

items.name: Definition 5.9 (governing triple)
items.statement: A triple (C, (ψ_{s+1}(x))_{x∈C−{x₀}}, χ_a) of type 2 is governing if (1) φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈T}; p_{s+1}(1)p_{s+1}(2)}(𝔊) exists for each T ⊆ [s]; (2) ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s−|T|+1}(x) = φ_{{p_i(1)p_i(2) : i∈[s]−T}; p_{s+1}(1)p_{s+1}(2)}(𝔊) for each nonempty T ⊆ [s]; (3) ∑_{x∈C_T} ψ_{s−|T|+1}(x) = 0 for each T ⊆ [s+1] with s+1 ∈ T.

items.name: Definition 6.1 (additive system)
items.statement: Let X_1, …, X_r be nonempty finite sets, X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r and S ⊆ [r]. An additive system on (X, S) is a tuple (C_T, C_T^{acc}, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} with: C_T^{acc} ⊆ C_T ⊆ Cube(X, T) (printed reversed), F_T: C_T → A_T a function, A_T a finite 𝔽₂-vector space; C_T^{acc} = {x̄ ∈ C_T : F_T(x̄) = 0}, and C_T = {x̄ ∈ Cube(X, T) : x̄(T − {i}) ⊆ C^{acc}_{T−{i}} for all i ∈ T} for ∅ ≠ T ⊆ S; and whenever x̄₁, x̄₂, x̄₃ ∈ C_T, i ∈ T and p₁, p₂, p₃ ∈ X_i satisfy π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₁) = π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₂) = π_{[r]−{i}}(x̄₃), π_i(x̄₁) = (p₁, p₂), π_i(x̄₂) = (p₂, p₃), π_i(x̄₃) = (p₁, p₃), then F_T(x̄₁) + F_T(x̄₂) = F_T(x̄₃) (equation (6.1)).

items.name: Degenerate cubes, the map Σ and Add(X, S)
items.statement: Let X = X_1 × ⋯ × X_r, S ⊆ [r], V = Map(X, 𝔽₂), W = Map(Cube(X, S), 𝔽₂). x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) is degenerate if pr₁(π_i(x̄)) = pr₂(π_i(x̄)) for some i ∈ S. Σ: V → W is the linear map ΣF(x̄) = ∑_{x∈x̄(∅)} F(x) if x̄ is not degenerate and 0 if x̄ is degenerate; Add(X, S) := im Σ. For Y ⊆ X, Σ: Map(Y, 𝔽₂) → Map(Cube(X, S), 𝔽₂) is ΣF(x̄) = ∑_{x∈x̄(∅)} F(x) if x̄ is not degenerate and x̄(∅) ⊆ Y, and 0 otherwise (printed: 'if x̄ is degenerate').

items.name: C(𝔄) and (a, S)-acceptable additive systems
items.statement: For an additive system 𝔄 = (C_T, C_T^{acc}, F_T, A_T)_{T⊆S} on (X, S), C(𝔄) := ⋂_{i∈S} {x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) : x̄(S − {i}) ∩ C^{acc}_{S−{i}} ≠ ∅}. 𝔄 is (a, S)-acceptable if |A_T| ≤ a for all T ⊆ S and x̄ ∈ C(𝔄) implies x̄(∅) ⊆ C_∅^{acc}.

items.name: K(X) and existence of cube expansion maps φ_{x̄; d}
items.statement: For nonempty finite sets X_1, …, X_r of odd primes, K(X_1 × ⋯ × X_r) is the compositum of the ℚ(√p), p ∈ ⋃_j X_j. For x̄ ∈ Cube(X, S) and an integer d ≠ 1 coprime to all elements of X, φ_{x̄; d} exists if x̄ is degenerate or if φ_{{pr₁(π_i(x̄))·pr₂(π_i(x̄)) : i ∈ S}; d}(𝔊) exists; for degenerate x̄ its field of definition is ℚ.

items.name: Basis(X, T) and the commutator operator β_j
items.statement: Enumerate X_k = {p_{k,1}, …, p_{k,|X_k|}} and set T_{k,l} = {p_{k,l}, p_{k,l+1}} (l ∈ [|X_k| − 1]). For T ⊆ [r] − {i}, Basis(X, T) is the set of x̄ ∈ Cube(X, T ∪ {i}) with {pr₁(π_k(x̄)), pr₂(π_k(x̄))} = T_{k,l} for some l, for every k ∈ T ∪ {i}; x̄₁ ∼ x̄₂ if these pairs agree as sets for all k. For φ ∈ Map(G_{M_j}, 𝔽₂) and σ₁, …, σ_{j+2} ∈ G_ℚ, β_jφ := φ([σ₁, [σ₂, [⋯[σ_{j+1}, σ_{j+2}]]]]), well defined since Gal(M_j/ℚ) has nilpotency class j + 1 (M_j := ∏_{|S′|=j} M_{S′}).

items.name: Standing convention for §§7–8: product spaces of primes read as squarefree integers
items.statement: X₁, …, X_r are pairwise disjoint, non-empty sets of primes, every prime ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r. The map X → 𝒟, (x₁, …, x_r) ↦ x₁⋯x_r, is injective, and an element of X is identified with the squarefree integer x₁⋯x_r. Here 𝒟 is the set of squarefree d > 0 all of whose prime divisors are ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and 𝒟(N) = {d ∈ 𝒟 : d < N}.

items.name: N-nice elements of 𝒟 (Definition 7.1)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 10^1000 and d ∈ 𝒟, with prime divisors p₁ < ⋯ < p_r. Put D₁ := e^{(log log N)^{1/10}} and C₀ := √(log log log N). Then d is N-nice if all three hold: (1) p_i > D₁ implies 2p_i < p_{i+1}; (2) (7.1) |½ log log p_i − i| < C₀^{1/5} · max(i, C₀)^{4/5} for all 1 ≤ i < r/3; (3) there is an i with r^{1/2}/2 < i < r/2 and log p_i ≥ (log log p_i)² · log log log N · Σ_{j=1}^{i−1} log p_j.

items.name: 𝒟_r(N) and ω(d)
items.statement: ω(d) is the number of distinct prime divisors of d, and 𝒟_r(N) := {d ∈ 𝒟(N) : ω(d) = r}.

items.name: Prebox (Definition 7.3)
items.statement: A prebox is a pair (X, P), where P, X₁, …, X_r are pairwise disjoint sets of primes, all ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4), and X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r, such that there are reals 2 < s₁ < t₁ < s₂ < t₂ < ⋯ < s_r < t_r with X_i ⊆ (s_i, t_i] for all i ∈ [r] and P ⊆ (1, s₁].

items.name: The isomorphism ι : 𝔽₂ → {±1}
items.statement: ι is the unique group isomorphism from (𝔽₂, +) to ({±1}, ·), namely ι(0) = 1 and ι(1) = −1.

items.name: Symbol index sets M_r, M_{r,P} and the fibre X(a) (Definition 7.4)
items.statement: Let (X, P) be a prebox. Put M_r := {(i, j) : i, j ∈ [r], i < j} and M_{r,P} := [r] × P. For subsets ℳ_r ⊆ M_r and ℳ_{r,P} ⊆ M_{r,P} and a map a : ℳ_r ⊔ ℳ_{r,P} → 𝔽₂, X(a) is the set of (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X with (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(i, j)) for all (i, j) ∈ ℳ_r and (x_i/p) = ι(a(i, p)) for all (i, p) ∈ ℳ_{r,P}. Here (·/·) is the Legendre symbol.

items.name: Siegel-free preboxes
items.statement: A prebox (X, P) is Siegel-free above a real t > 0 if there are no index i with |d_i| > t and no x ∈ X such that d_i divides x · ∏_{p∈P} p. Here d₁, d₂, … enumerate 𝒮(c_Landau).

items.name: Key step in Proposition 7.6: the induction that moves x₁ into P, (7.12)–(7.16)
items.statement: Split ||X(a)| − |X|/2^{|ℳ_r|}| by the value of x₁ (7.12). For bad x₁, apply the induction hypothesis to the prebox (X₂ × ⋯ × X_k × X_{k+1}(a, x₁) × ⋯ × X_r(a, x₁), P ∪ {x₁}). Take k_new ≥ k − 1 minimal with t_{k_new+2} > max(e^{(log t₂)^{c₅}}, e^{t^{c₆}}), and k_new = r − 1 if there is none. This gives (7.13): Σ_{x ∈ X(a), π₁(x) ∈ X₁^bad} 1 ≤ k · 2^{−|ℳ_r|+k+1} · |X|/t₁^{c₉} ≤ |X| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} · 2^{|ℳ_r|+2}). For good x₁, apply it to X(x₁) := X₂(a, x₁) × ⋯ × X_r(a, x₁) with P ∪ {x₁}. With M the number of pairs (1, j) ∈ ℳ_r, this gives (7.14) ||X(x₁)(a)| − |X(x₁)|/2^{|ℳ_r|−M}| ≤ (r − 1)|X(x₁)| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} 2^{|ℳ_r|−M}) and (7.15) |2^M|X(x₁)| − |X|/|X₁|| ≤ |X| / (100 t₁^{c₈+1/c₁}|X₁|). Hence (7.16): the good part is within (r − ¼)|X| / (t₁^{c₈+1/c₁} 2^{|ℳ_r|}) of |X|/2^{|ℳ_r|}.

items.name: Permutations 𝒫_r, 𝒫_r(k) and their action σ(a) on symbol maps
items.statement: 𝒫_r is the set of permutations of [r], and 𝒫_r(k) := {σ ∈ 𝒫_r : σ(i) = i for all i > k}. For a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,P} → 𝔽₂ set a(j, i) := a(i, j) for j > i, and define σ(a)(i, j) := a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j)) and σ(a)(i, p) := a(σ⁻¹(i), p).

items.name: Truncated fibres X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a) and the count C(k₀, k₁)
items.statement: For integers k₁ ≥ k₀ ≥ 0, X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a) is the set of x = (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X such that (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j))) for all i, j ∈ [k₁] with σ⁻¹(i) < σ⁻¹(j) and min(i, j) ≤ k₀, and (x_i/p) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), p)) for all (i, p) ∈ [k₁] × P. The number of such pairs {i, j} is C(k₀, k₁) := ½(k₀² − k₀) + k₀(k₁ − k₀), which does not depend on σ.

items.name: Key steps in Proposition 7.8: trimmed factors, the good case and bad pairs, (7.19)–(7.23)
items.statement: Reduce to X_i = {x_i} for i ∈ [k₀]. Lemma 7.7 and Cauchy–Schwarz give (7.19): the replacement of Σ_σ |X(σ(a))| by Σ_σ |X^trun_{k₀,k₁}(σ, a)| / 2^{|M_r ⊔ M_{r,P}| − C(k₀,k₁) − k₁|P|} costs at most k₂!|X| / (2k₂^{c₁₂}). For i > k₀ let X_i^trim(σ, a) := {x_i ∈ X_i : (x_i/p) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), p)) for all p ∈ P, and (x_i/x_j) = ι(a(σ⁻¹(i), σ⁻¹(j))) for all j ∈ [k₀]}. The Chebotarev density theorem gives (7.20): ||X_i^trim(σ, a)| − |X_i|/2^{k₀+|P|}| ≤ |X_i|/t_{k₀+1} for all i > k₁. If |X′_i| ≥ |X_{i+k₀}| / (2^{k₀+|P|} k₂^{c₉}) for all i, where X′ is X^trun viewed as a prebox with P′ = P ∪ {x₁, …, x_{k₀}}, then Proposition 7.6 applied to (X^trim_{k₀+1} × ⋯ × X^trim_r, P′) gives (7.21). Otherwise (σ, a) is bad at some i ∈ [k₁ − k₀]; grouping a into the ≤ 2^{k₀+|P|} classes of ∼_{σ,j} gives (7.22), and the good pairs give (7.23).

items.name: The Siegel threshold D_Siegel
items.statement: D_Siegel := e^{(log log N)^{1/100}} (to be compared with D₁ = e^{(log log N)^{1/10}} from Definition 7.1).

items.name: (N, k, r)-boxes X(𝐭) (Definition 7.9)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 10^1000, let r be a positive integer, let 0 ≤ k ≤ r, and let C_compr be a real with 100 ≤ C_compr ≤ (log N)^100. Let 𝐭 = (p₁, …, p_k, s_{k+1}, …, s_r), where the p_i are primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) and the s_j are reals, with p₁ < ⋯ < p_k < D₁ ≤ s_{k+1} < ⋯ < s_r and s_i < (2/3) s_{i+1} for all k < i < r. Then X(𝐭) := X₁ × ⋯ × X_r with X_i = {p_i} for 1 ≤ i ≤ k, and X_i the set of primes ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) in (s_i, s_i(1 + 1/C_compr)] for k < i ≤ r. A product space X is an (N, k, r)-box if X = X(𝐭) for some 𝐭 and X ⊆ 𝒟(N).

items.name: Excellent boxes
items.statement: An (N, k, r)-box X is excellent if some d ∈ X is N-nice and {α ∏_{i∈S} π_i(x) : x ∈ X, S ⊆ [r], α ∈ {1, −1}, |α ∏_{i∈S} π_i(x)| > D_Siegel} ∩ 𝒮(c_Landau) = ∅.

items.name: Fixed choice C_compr := (log log N)^{50}
items.statement: From §7.3 on, C_compr := (log log N)^{50}. Theorem 7.10 holds equally with any congruence conditions on the radicands, such as odd or even radicands, so all proofs also work when ordering by discriminant.

items.name: Proof of Theorem 7.13: Proposition 7.8 on excellent boxes, (7.24)–(7.25)
items.statement: Let W be the set of N-nice d ∈ 𝒟_r(N) lying in no W(d_i) with |d_i| > D_Siegel. Theorem 7.2 and Proposition 7.12 with t = D_Siegel give |𝒟_r(N)| − |W| ≪ |𝒟_r(N)| e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}. By Theorem 7.10 it suffices to show (7.24): |D_{2,n} ∩ X| / |X| = P_Sym(r − 1, n) + O(e^{−(log log log N)^{1/4}}) for every excellent (N, k, r)-box X. Apply Proposition 7.8 to (X, ∅) with (c₁, …, c₁₂) = (100, 10^{−9}, 5, 10^6, 5, 5, 1/100, 1/100, 5, 1/5, 1/5, 1/5), k₀ = k, k₁ the least integer with t_{k₁+1} > max(e^{(log t_{k+1})^5}, e^{t^5}), and k₂ = r. Its hypotheses follow from (7.1) and (7.4) for N large. The result is (7.25): Σ_{a : M_r → 𝔽₂} |r! · |X| / 2^{r(r−1)/2} − Σ_{σ∈𝒫_r} |X(σ(a))|| ≤ r! · |X| · (r^{−1/5} + t_{k+1}^{−1/100}). With (7.27) and the permutation invariance of dim ker A(a), this gives (7.24).

items.name: The Rédei matrix A(a) and the reduced matrix A′(a), (7.26)
items.statement: For a : M_r → 𝔽₂ let A(a) be the r × r matrix over 𝔽₂ whose (i, j) entry is a(i, j) = a(j, i) for i ≠ j, with diagonal (7.26) a(i, i) := Σ_{k≠i} a(i, k). Then A(a) is symmetric with all row sums 0, and a ↦ A(a) is a bijection from maps M_r → 𝔽₂ onto symmetric r × r matrices with zero row sums. Deleting the last row and column gives A′(a), and a ↦ A′(a) is a bijection onto all symmetric (r − 1) × (r − 1) matrices. For σ ∈ 𝒫_r, dim ker A(σ(a)) = dim ker A(a).

items.name: D_{k,n}, D_{k,n}(N) and P(m, n, j)
items.statement: For k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 0, D_{k,n} := {d ∈ 𝒟 : rk_{2^k} Cl(ℚ(√d)) = n and (√d) ∈ 2^{k−1} Cl(ℚ(√d))}, with Cl the narrow class group and rk_{2^k} A = dim_{𝔽₂} 2^{k−1}A[2^k]. D_{k,n}(N) := {d ∈ D_{k,n} : d < N}. P(m, n, j) is the probability that a uniformly random m × n matrix over 𝔽₂ has right kernel of dimension j.

items.name: The constants A_Comb and c
items.statement: A_Comb > 0 is a real number for which Proposition 6.6 (Smith's equidistribution theorem for acceptable additive systems) holds, and c := 1/(A_Comb · 10^{10}).

items.name: Stevenhagen's conditional densities P₂^±(m), P₂(m), P₃(m, n)
items.statement: For integers m ≥ 0: P₂^−(m) := liminf_{X→∞} |𝒟^−(X) ∩ D_{2,m}(X)| / |D_{2,m}(X)| and P₂^+(m) := limsup_{X→∞} of the same ratio. P₂(m) is their common value when they agree. For m ≥ n ≥ 0, P₃(m, n) := lim_{X→∞} |𝒟^−(X) ∩ D_{2,m}(X) ∩ D_{3,n}(X)| / |D_{2,m}(X) ∩ D_{3,n}(X)| when the limit exists.

items.name: The gap index k_gap of an excellent box, (8.3)
items.statement: Let X be an excellent (N, k, r)-box. Fix x = (x₁, …, x_r) ∈ X and an integer k_gap with r^{1/2}/2 < k_gap + 1 < r/2 and (8.3) log x_{k_gap+1} ≥ (log log x_{k_gap+1})² · log log log N · Σ_{j=1}^{k_gap} log x_j. These exist by the third condition of N-niceness.

items.name: a-consistency, X(a, Q) and X_j(a, Q) (Definition 8.3)
items.statement: Let X = X₁ × ⋯ × X_r be a product space, S ⊆ [r], Q ∈ ∏_{i∈S} X_i and a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂ (with a(j, i) := a(i, j)). Q is a-consistent if (π_i(Q)/π_j(Q)) = ι(a(i, j)) for all distinct i, j ∈ S. X(a, Q) := {x ∈ X(a) : π_S(x) = Q}. For j ∈ [r] − S, X_j(a, Q) := {p ∈ X_j : (π_i(Q)/p) = ι(a(i, j)) for all i ∈ S}.

items.name: The kernel V_{a,2}, the vector R and (N, m)-generic maps (Definition 8.4)
items.statement: For a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂, V_{a,2} ⊆ 𝔽₂^r is the kernel of the symmetric matrix A(a) of (7.26). Its left and right kernels coincide and contain R := (1, …, 1). a is (N, m)-generic for a box X if three conditions hold. (1) (8.4) dim V_{a,2} ≤ n_max := ⌊√((10c / (m² 6^m)) · log log log log log N)⌋. (2) (8.5) |X_j(a, Q)| ≥ |X_j| / (log s_{k+1})^{100} for all j > k, where Q is the unique element of X₁ × ⋯ × X_k, and Q is a-consistent. (3) Let α_pre := #{i ∈ ℤ : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap}. For all w ∈ V_{a,2} ∖ ⟨R⟩ and all j ∈ 𝔽₂: (8.6) ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap, π_i(w) = j}| − α_pre/2| ≤ k_gap / log log log N, and (8.7) ||{i ∈ [r] : k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap, π_i(w) = j}| − k_gap/2| ≤ k_gap / log log log N.

items.name: Valid and Pellian sequences of pairings (Definition 8.6)
items.statement: Let X be a box and a : M_r ⊔ M_{r,∅} → 𝔽₂. A sequence of bilinear pairings {Art_i : A_i × B_i → 𝔽₂}_{2≤i<m} is valid if A₂ = B₂ = V_{a,2}; the left kernel of Art_i is A_{i+1} and its right kernel is B_{i+1} for 2 ≤ i < m − 1; and R is in the right kernel of Art_i for 2 ≤ i < m. It is Pellian if moreover R is in the left kernel of Art_i for all 2 ≤ i < m. A_m and B_m are the left and right kernels of Art_{m−1}.

items.name: The sequence of Artin pairings of x ∈ X(a), and X(a, {Art_i})
items.statement: For x ∈ X and k ≥ 1, Art_{k,x} : 2^{k−1}Cl(ℚ(√x))[2^k] × 2^{k−1}Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[2^k] → 𝔽₂ is the Artin pairing of §2.3. Pull Art_{1,x} back along the genus-theory surjections to a pairing 𝔽₂^r × 𝔽₂^r → 𝔽₂. For x ∈ X(a) its left and right kernels both equal V_{a,2}, which gives surjections V_{a,2} → 2Cl(ℚ(√x))[4] and V_{a,2} → 2Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[4] and a pairing V_{a,2} × V_{a,2} → 𝔽₂. Iterating gives a valid sequence {Art_{i,x}}_{i≥2}. For a valid sequence {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}, X(a, {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}) := {x ∈ X(a) : the Artin pairings of x equal {Art_i}_{2≤i<m}}.

items.name: Adapted bases and the matrix of Art_{m,x} (Definition 8.9, first part)
items.statement: For 2 ≤ i ≤ m, C_i := A_i ∩ B_i, d_i := dim_{𝔽₂} C_i − 1 and n_i := dim_{𝔽₂} A_i − 1. Choose a basis v₁, …, v_{n_m}, R of A_m and a basis w₁, …, w_{n_m}, R of B_m with v_i = w_i for 1 ≤ i ≤ d_m, so that v₁, …, v_{d_m}, R is a basis of C_m. Extend to a basis w₁, …, w_{n₂}, R of V_{a,2} such that w₁, …, w_{n_i}, R is a basis of B_i for every 2 ≤ i ≤ m. Mat(a, b, K) is the set of a × b matrices over a field K. Art_{m,x} becomes the matrix in Mat(n_m + 1, n_m + 1, 𝔽₂) with (i, j) entry Art_{m,x}(v_i, w_j) for i, j ∈ [n_m], whose last row and column record pairing with R. Since R is in the right kernel, it is also viewed in Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂).

items.name: The four cases I–IV of a non-trivial functional F (Definition 8.9, second part)
items.statement: E_{j₃,j₄} is the matrix unit and F_{j₁,j₂} : Mat(n_m + 1, n_m, 𝔽₂) → 𝔽₂ is the linear map sending E_{j₃,j₄} to 1 exactly when (j₃, j₄) = (j₁, j₂). Every F is Σ_{1≤j₁≤n_m+1, 1≤j₂≤n_m} c_{j₁,j₂} F_{j₁,j₂}. For F ≠ 0 choose (j₁, j₂) with c_{j₁,j₂} = 1 by the first case that applies. Case I: j₁ ≤ n_m and one of n_m ≥ j₁ > d_m, n_m ≥ j₂ > d_m, or (1 ≤ j₁, j₂ ≤ d_m and c_{j₂,j₁} = 0). Case II: c_{n_m+1,j} = 1 for some j, and (j₁, j₂) := (n_m + 1, j). Case III: c_{j,j} = 1 for some j, and (j₁, j₂) := (j, j). Case IV: some j₁ ≠ j₂ with c_{j₁,j₂} = c_{j₂,j₁} = 1, which always exists when F ≠ 0 and Cases I–III fail.

items.name: Sets of variable indices S for F and the index i_Cheb (Definition 8.9, third part)
items.statement: Put G := {i : k_gap/2 ≤ i ≤ k_gap}, H := {i : k_gap < i ≤ 2k_gap} and Z₀ := G ∩ ⋂_{l=1}^{n₂} {i ∈ [r] : π_i(w_l) = 0}. S is a set of variable indices for F if, according to its case: Case I: |S| = m + 1, with m − 1 elements in Z₀; one element in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₂ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₂)} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1}; and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₁} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₁ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₁)} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(v_{j₁}) = 1}. Case II: |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in Z₀ and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, (j₂ ≤ d_m ⇒ l ≠ j₂)} {π_i(v_l) = 0} ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1}. Case III (j = j₁ = j₂): |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n₂, l ≠ j} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_j) = 1} and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m} {π_i(v_l) = π_i(w_l) = 0}. Case IV: |S| = m, with m − 1 elements in G ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n₂, l ≠ j₂} {π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(w_{j₂}) = 1} and one element in H ∩ ⋂_{l ≤ n_m, l ≠ j₁} {π_i(v_l) = π_i(w_l) = 0} ∩ {π_i(v_{j₁}) = 1}. i_Cheb is the unique element of S ∩ H.

items.name: The fibre X(a, Q, {Art_k}) over the fixed small non-variable primes
items.statement: For Q ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [k_gap] − S} X_i, X(a, Q, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) := {x ∈ X(a, {Art_k}_{2≤k<m}) : π_{[k_gap]−S}(x) = Q}.

items.name: M_box, S′ and great product spaces (Definition 8.11)
items.statement: Put M_box := ⌊(log log log log N)^{1/(5(m+1))}⌋; by (8.13), M_box ≥ 2 for N large. Put S′ := S ∩ [k_gap], so S = S′ ∪ {i_Cheb}. For Z_i ⊆ X_i (i ∈ S′), Z := ∏_{i∈S′} Z_i is a great product space if all of the following hold. (1) |Z_i| = M_box and Z_i ⊆ X_i(a, Q) for all i ∈ S′. (2) (π_i(z)/π_j(z)) = ι(a(i, j)) for all z ∈ Z and all distinct i, j ∈ S′. (3) In Case I, let i_char be the unique index in S′ with π_{i_char}(w_{j₂}) = 1. For all T ⊆ S′ − {i_char} and all z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T ∪ {i_char}), the expansion map φ_{π_T(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))} exists, and when T ⊊ S′ − {i_char} all primes of Q, (2) and ∞ split completely in it. (4) In Cases II–IV: for all T ⊆ S′, z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T) and i ∈ T, the map φ_{π_{T−{i}}(z̄); pr₁(π_i(z̄)) pr₂(π_i(z̄))} exists with all primes of Q, (2) and ∞ split completely in it. Also, for all T ⊆ S′ and z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T), the map φ_{π_T(z̄); −1} exists, and when T ⊊ S′ all odd primes of Q and Up_{ℚ(i)/ℚ}(2) split completely in it.

items.name: The fields M_∘(Z), M(Z), the sets X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) and the space Z̃
items.statement: In Case I: M_∘(Z) := ∏_{T ⊊ S′−{i_char}} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T∪{i_char})} L(φ_{π_T(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))}), and M(Z) := ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′−{i_char}}(z̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(z̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(z̄))}). In Cases II–IV: M_∘(Z) := ∏_{i∈S′} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′−{i}}(z̄); pr₁(π_i(z̄)) pr₂(π_i(z̄))}) · ∏_{T ⊊ S′} ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, T)} L(φ_{π_T(z̄); −1}), and M(Z) := ∏_{z̄ ∈ Cube(Z, S′)} L(φ_{π_{S′}(z̄); −1}). Products of fields are composita. For i > k_gap, X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) is the set of p ∈ X_i(a, Q) that split completely in M_∘(Z) and satisfy (z/p) = ι(a(j, i)) for all j ∈ S′ and all z ∈ Z_j. This is a condition that Frob_p equal a given central element of the Galois group of M_∘(Z) · ℚ(√z : z ∈ {−1} ∪ {primes of Q} ∪ ⋃_j Z_j). For a great Z, Z̃ := Q × Z × ∏_{i>k_gap} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)).

items.name: The pre-space X_pre
items.statement: X_pre := ∏_{i∈S′} X_i(a, Q).

items.name: Theorem 8.13 implies Theorem 8.10, step 1: a cover by great product spaces, and (8.17)
items.statement: Set R := ⌊e^{e^{k_gap/5}}⌋ (the letter R is reused) and let Z_pre be the set of a-consistent z ∈ X_pre. Choose a sequence Z₁, …, Z_t of maximal length with each Z_i ⊆ Z_pre great, |Z_i ∩ Z_j| ≤ 1 for i ≠ j, and each z ∈ Z_pre in at most R of the Z_i. Let Z_pre,bad be the set of z in fewer than R of the Z_i, and δ its density in X_pre. A greedy choice gives W ⊆ Z_pre,bad of density ≥ δ/(R M_box^m) with |W ∩ Z_i| ≤ 1. Proposition 6.2 with Lemma 8.12 gives C_{S′}^acc density ≥ δ′ := (δ / (2^{(|S′|+100)(k_gap+|S′|+100)} R M_box^m))^{3^m}. Via the injection of C_{S′}^acc into ⊔_{x₀∈W} W(x₀), some W(x₀) has density ≥ δ′. Maximality and the contrapositive of Lemma 6.3 then give 5 M_box^m > log min_{i∈S′} |X_i(a, Q)| / log δ′^{−1}. With |X_i(a, Q)| ≥ e^{e^{(3/10)k_gap}}, from (8.14) and (7.1), this yields (8.17) δ ≤ e^{−¼ e^{k_gap}}.

items.name: Raw cocycles ψ_i(x, v) attached to kernel vectors
items.statement: For every non-zero v ∈ V_{a,2} and every x ∈ X(a, Q), fix a raw cocycle (ψ_i(x, v))_{0≤i≤t(x,v)} for N(x) with ψ₁(x, v) = Σ_{1≤j≤r, π_j(v)=1} χ_{π_j(x)} and t(x, v) maximal among such raw cocycles. Also set n₁ := n₂.

items.name: Construction of F_T = (F_{T,1}, F_{T,2}, F_{T,3})
items.statement: Case I; the other cases are similar. Induct on |T|, with F_T := 0 if T = ∅ or |T| ≥ m. For 0 < |T| < m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n_{|T|+1} (with T ⊆ S′ − {i_char} if j > n_m) and x̄ ∈ C_T, let ψ(x̄, j) := Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|}(x, w_j). Add φ_{π_{T−{i_char}}(x̄); pr₁(π_{i_char}(x̄)) pr₂(π_{i_char}(x̄))} when j = j₂ and i_char ∈ T, and set ψ(x̄, j₁) := 0 when i_Cheb ∈ T and j₁ ∈ 𝒲. By Proposition 2.9, dψ(x̄, j) = 0, and ψ(x̄, j) is an unramified quadratic character of ℚ(√x) in which Up(π_j(x̄)) splits for j ∉ T. By (8.7) there are an injection f : [n₂] → [r] − S − {1} with π_{f(i)}(w_j) = 1 ⟺ i = j, and some i₀ ∈ [r] − S − {1} with π_{i₀}(w_j) = 0 for all j ∈ [n₂]. For any x₀ ∈ x̄(∅), put F_{T,1}(x̄) := (ψ(x̄, j)(Frob(Up_{ℚ(√x₀)/ℚ}(π_i(x₀)))))_{j ≤ n_{|T|+1}, i ∈ T}; F_{T,2}(x̄) := ((ψ(x̄, j)(σ_{π_{i₀}(x₀)}))_j, (ψ(x̄, j)(σ_{π_{f(i)}(x₀)}))_{j, i∈[n₂]}); F_{T,3}(x̄) := (Σ_{x∈x̄(∅)} ψ_{|T|+1}(x, w_j)(σ_{π_i(x₀)}))_{j, i∈S−T}. For T ⊄ S′ − {i_char}, j runs only up to n_m in F_{T,1} and F_{T,2}. Each part is independent of x₀ and satisfies (6.1), so F_T defines an additive system with |A_T| ≤ 2^{(n_max+10)(n_max+2m+10)}.

items.name: Q_post, Z̃(Q_post), even distribution over Chebotarev classes, and evenly distributed candidates
items.statement: For Q_post ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [r]−[k_gap], i ≠ i_Cheb} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)), Z̃(Q_post) := {x ∈ Z̃ : π_{[r]−[k_gap]−{i_Cheb}}(x) = Q_post}. Q_post is unevenly distributed over the Chebotarev classes if for some σ ∈ Gal(M_∘(Z) M(Z) / M_∘(Z)), ||X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z), σ)| − |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z))| / 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}}| ≥ |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_post, M_∘(Z))| / (e^{0.5 k_gap} · 2^{(M_box−1)^{|S′|}}); otherwise it is evenly distributed. An element Q_{j,post} ∈ ∏_{i ∈ [j]−[k_gap], i ≠ i_Cheb} X_i(a, Q, M_∘(Z)) is an evenly distributed candidate if two conditions hold. First, when j − 1 > k_gap, π_{[j−1]−[k_gap]}(Q_{j,post}) is an evenly distributed candidate. Second, when j ≠ i_Cheb, |Σ_{p ∈ X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_{j−1,post}, M_∘(Z), σ)} (p / π_j(Q_{j,post}))| ≤ |X_{i_Cheb}(a, Q × Q_{j−1,post}, M_∘(Z), σ)| / |X_{k_gap+1}(a, Q, M_∘(Z))|^{1/100} for all σ.

items.name: Period and splitting-degree index of a class
items.statement: For α∈Br(K), per(α) is its positive finite order and ind(α) is the minimum degree of a finite splitting extension, equivalently the gcd of their degrees. Descend item04 to Brauer classes and prove both comparisons, using item05 only for attainment.

items.name: Weighted box and polydisc for a torsion ideal
items.statement: Given K of degree n, m ≥ 1, a nonzero integral ideal I and I^m = (α) with α ≠ 0, set R_v = D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m). The product of real intervals [-R_v,R_v] and closed complex discs of radius R_v is compact, symmetric and convex, with volume 2^r pi^s sqrt(D_K)/N(I).

items.name: Reduced integral basis starting with one
items.statement: For every degree-n number field with n≥2, there is a Z-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n−1) of O_K, nondecreasing in the trace-weighted Euclidean norm, such that ||v_i||_tr≤(3/2)^i||w||_tr for every 1≤i≤n−1 and integral w outside span_Q(1,v_1,...,v_(i−1)). The product Π_(i=1)^(n−1)||v_i||_tr is bounded above and below by positive degree-dependent multiples of sqrt(D_K).

items.name: Top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and a basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1), form the symmetric (n−2)-square rational matrix A whose entry a_ij is the coefficient of v_(n−1) in v_i v_j, for 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n−2.

items.name: Injecting 2-torsion into balanced square-norm elements
items.statement: For K of degree n set R = D_K^(1/n) and B_K(R) = {β ∈ O_K : |β|_v ≤ R for every infinite v}. Choosing the order-dividing-m=2 representatives defines an injection Cl(K)[2] → {β ∈ B_K(R) : β ≠ 0 and |N_K/Q(β)| is an integer square}.

items.name: The monic integral norm polynomial
items.statement: For β ∈ O_K define P_β(X) as the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by β on the free Z-module O_K. It is monic in Z[X], has degree [K:Q], and satisfies P_β(t) = N_K/Q(t−β) for t ∈ Q.

items.name: Both norm signs in a bounded norm-curve rectangle
items.statement: For K of degree n ≥ 3, R = D_K^(1/n), β_0 ∈ B_K(R) and α = β_0−m ∈ B_K(R) with m ∈ Z, α ≠ 0 and |N(α)| = y² for y ∈ Z_≥0, one has |m| ≤ 2R and 0 < y ≤ sqrt(D_K). The assignment α ↦ (s,m,y), with s chosen so that y² = sP_β0(m), injects into the union of the two norm curves in this rectangle.

items.name: Packing and feedback constants
items.statement: Put u=√3/2, b=((1+u)/(2u)) log((1+u)/(2u))−((1−u)/(2u)) log((1−u)/(2u)), a=1/(6(1−b/log 2)), c=ab/log 2. All logarithms except log₂ are natural.

items.name: Elliptic curves from cubic norm polynomials
items.statement: The balanced translation cosets for a cubic field give O(D_K^(1/6)) signed equations ±y²=x³+Ax²+Bx+C with |A|≪D_K^(1/3), |B|≪D_K^(2/3), |C|≪D_K; counted points have |x|≪D_K^(1/3), |y|≪D_K^(1/2).

items.name: Class group of a finite étale rational algebra
items.statement: For A=∏ K_i a finite étale Q-algebra, Cl(A)=∏Cl(O_(K_i)), h₂(A)=∏h₂(K_i), and D_A=∏|disc K_i|. These use maximal orders, not an arbitrary polynomial order.

items.name: Cubic étale resolvent of a quartic field
items.statement: For a quartic field K, let its Galois group act on the three partitions of the four embeddings into two unordered pairs. The associated degree-three finite étale Q-algebra is its cubic resolvent A.

items.name: Common nontrivial factor of the permutation modules
items.statement: Let M=F₂^4 with S₄ permuting its basis, M₀ the line spanned by the sum, M₁=M/M₀ and M₂ the image of the even-weight subspace in M₁. Let N=F₂^3 on the three pair partitions and N₀ its sum line. Then M₁/M₂ is trivial and N/N₀≅M₂ equivariantly.

items.name: Discriminant-negligible comparison
items.statement: For bounded degree n of a Galois splitting field L and bounded torus dimension d, a positive quantity F is negligible if for every ε>0, D_L^(-ε)≪_(n,d,ε) F≪_(n,d,ε)D_L^ε.

items.name: Trace-weighted Euclidean metric on the mixed embedding
items.statement: For a number field K of signature (r,s) and degree n=r+2s, put ||x||_tr²=Σ_real |x_v|²+2Σ_complex |x_v|² on its existing mixed space. The diagonal real map scaling both real coordinates of each complex factor by sqrt(2) identifies this metric with ordinary Euclidean space and has determinant 2^s. Thus ||x||_0≤||x||_tr≤sqrt(2)||x||_0, and the integer lattice has covolume sqrt(D_K) for the metric-induced Euclidean volume. The vector 1 is primitive and shortest, of trace length sqrt(n).

items.name: The class-field extension cut out by quadratic coinvariants
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F, let A=Cl(E)/2Cl(E), let σ be the induced involution, and put T=σ−1, V=A/TA and s=dim_F2 V. Then T²=0 and dim_F2 A≤2s. In the elementary-2 ordinary Hilbert class field H/E corresponding to A, the fixed field M=H^(TA) is Galois over F and yields a central exact sequence 1→V→G=Gal(M/F)→C2→1. The group G is abelian, has order 2^(s+1), and |2G|≤2; the sequence is not asserted to split without a ramified place.

items.name: Canonical measure comparison for the short-integer argument
items.statement: If K has signature (r1,s), n=r1+2s, put <x,y> = sum_real x_i y_i + sum_complex (x_j conjugate(y_j)+conjugate(x_j)y_j). Its Euclidean Haar measure mu_can equals 2^s times standard product Lebesgue measure. The sup unit ball has mu_can-volume 2^r1(2*pi)^s >= 2^n.

items.name: More than half a basis of small integral elements
items.statement: Minkowski second with mu_can gives Z-independent omega_1,...,omega_n in O_K with ordered gauges and product <= delta^(n/2). For m=floor(n/2)+1, the first m have gauge <= delta.

items.name: Integral parameters and evaluation maps
items.statement: For the independent short alpha_i and integers u_ij, set kappa_j=sum_i u_ij alpha_i. Define epsilon_Q:Q[x_1,...,x_r]->K by x_j |-> kappa_j and its real and complex base changes. In complex embedding coordinates P_tau=(sum_i u_ij tau(alpha_i))_j.

items.name: Saturated integral relation lattice
items.statement: Let W=ker(epsilon_R restricted to V_R), and L=W intersect V_Z=ker(epsilon_Z,d). Then L is saturated in Z^M, rank_Z L=ell=M-n, and its real span is W. Let Lperp=Wperp intersect Z^M.

items.name: Dual evaluation image and its finite index
items.statement: For Odual=Hom_Z(O_K,Z), the transpose of epsilon_Z,d maps Odual injectively into Lperp, and its image has full rank n. Hence covol(L)=covol(Lperp)<=covol(image(epsilon_Z,d^t)).

items.name: Independent integral relations with product bound
items.statement: Minkowski second on L supplies ell independent integral relations E_1,...,E_ell, ordered by coefficient Euclidean norm, with product_i ||E_i||_2 <= ell^(ell/2)*D^(n/2). Each nonzero E_i has norm at least one.

items.name: Jacobian-open component model
items.statement: For r polynomials E in Q[x_1,...,x_r], define X_E=Spec((Q[x]/(E_1,...,E_r))[1/J]), J=det(partial E_i/partial x_j). This is the open part of the common zero scheme on which J is invertible.

items.name: Logarithmic dimension and degree choice
items.statement: Let r be the least positive integer satisfying n(r+1)<=binom(2r,r), and set d=r. For all sufficiently large n one has r>=5, r<=3*log(n), and n(r+1)<=binom(2r,r)<=4*n*(r+1).

items.name: Nonzero sections with even divisor
items.statement: Fix a divisor E of degree g on C/k. Let V=L(2E), and S_E={f∈V:f≠0 and every coefficient of div(f) is even}. This is a k×-stable subset of V minus zero, not asserted to be a subspace.

items.name: Projective sections map to 2-torsion
items.statement: For f∈S_E, divide the coefficients of div(f) by two to obtain an integral degree-zero divisor A_f. The class [A_f] depends only on the projective class of f and satisfies 2[A_f]=0.

items.name: Gonality over the stated constant field
items.statement: The k-gonality of C is the minimum degree of a nonconstant k-morphism C→P¹. The second assertion only assumes existence of a degree-n map, not minimality.

items.name: Successive minima
items.statement: For a full lattice Λ in a positive-dimensional Euclidean real space with closed unit ball B, λ_i is the infimum of t > 0 such that Λ ∩ tB spans a real subspace of dimension at least i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.

items.name: Minkowski-reduced bases and the Siegel-set description
items.statement: A Z-basis α_1, …, α_n of a lattice L is Minkowski-reduced if, successively for i = 1, …, n, α_i is a shortest vector of L such that α_1, …, α_i extends to a Z-basis of L; most lattices have a unique one (up to signs). For a positive definite form Q = γI_nγ^T with γ = ντκ (ν lower unipotent, τ = diag(t_1, …, t_n), κ ∈ SO_n(R)), Minkowski-reduced forms lie in a Siegel set F_SL = {ντκ : ν ∈ N′, t_i ≤ ct_{i+1}}.

items.name: Singular symmetric matrices in skew balls; S(Λ), ℓ_i ∗ ℓ_j, C(r, s)
items.statement: S = Sym²(n) with the Euclidean length, S(Z)^{(r)} the rank-r integral matrices, s = diag(t_1^{−1}, …, t_n^{−1}) ∈ T′ with Y^{−Θ} ≪ t_n ≤ t_1 ≪ Y^Θ, and N_r(Y, s) = #(s(YD) ∩ S(Z)^{(r)}). C(r, s) = ∏_{i≤r}∏_{j≤n−i}t_j/t_{n−i+1} = ∏_{i<j, j>n−r}t_i/t_j ≪ δ(s)^{−1} (21). For a primitive rank-r Λ ⊂ Z^n, S(Λ) is the set of B ∈ S(Z) whose row space is a full-rank sublattice of Λ ⊗ R, and S′(Λ) is the lattice it spans. v_1 ∗ v_2 = v_1v_2^t + v_2v_1^t (or v_1v_2^t if they are dependent), with |v||w| ≤ |v ∗ w| ≤ 2|v||w| (24).

items.name: Minkowski-reduced bases
items.statement: A Z-basis of a lattice is Minkowski-reduced if each successive vector is a shortest vector extending the previous ones to part of a basis; a lattice generically has a unique such basis up to signs.

items.name: Integer orthogonal kernel
items.statement: For N≥1 and c∈Z^N let Lambda_c={y∈Z^N:<c,y>=0}. It is a saturated integral lattice; for c≠0 its rank is N−1.

items.name: Homogeneous angular band
items.statement: For N≥1, gamma>0 and v∈R^N, C_v^(gamma)={t:|<v,t>|≤||v|| ||t||/(2gamma)}.

items.name: Congruence kernel lattice
items.statement: For positive integer Q and c∈Z^N, Lambda_c^(Q)={y∈Z^N:<c,y>≡0 mod Q}. This has full rank, unlike Lambda_c for nonzero c.

items.name: Discrete lattice in its span
items.statement: A lattice Lambda⊂R^N is a discrete additive subgroup. Its rank R is dim_R span_R Lambda; regard Lambda as a full lattice in that span, including R=0.

items.name: Intrinsic covolume
items.statement: For a rank-R lattice and any Z-basis with column matrix B∈M_{N,R}(R), det(Lambda)=sqrt(det(B^t B)), with empty determinant 1. This is intrinsic R-dimensional covolume.

items.name: Orthogonal quotient lattice
items.statement: If Gamma≤Lambda and span_R(Gamma)∩Lambda=Gamma, let Lambda/Gamma=pi(Lambda), where pi is orthogonal projection to span_R(Gamma)^perp. It is a lattice of rank rank(Lambda)−rank(Gamma), with covolume det(Lambda)/det(Gamma).

items.name: Primitive integral lattice
items.statement: An integral lattice is a lattice Lambda⊂Z^N; it is primitive iff span_R(Lambda)∩Z^N=Lambda, equivalently it is not properly contained in another integral lattice of the same rank.

items.name: Integral orthogonal lattice
items.statement: Lambda^perp={a∈Z^N:∀z∈Lambda,<a,z>=0}. It is primitive of rank N−rank Lambda. Double perpendicular is the saturation; for primitive Lambda it equals Lambda and det(Lambda^perp)=det(Lambda).

items.name: Euclidean dual lattice
items.statement: For Lambda⊂R^N define Lambda*={a∈span_R Lambda:∀z∈Lambda,<a,z>∈Z}. It has the same rank and det(Lambda*)=det(Lambda)^{-1}. The ambient space restriction is essential.

items.name: Successive Euclidean minima
items.statement: For 1≤R≤N and rank-R Lambda⊂R^N, lambda_i(Lambda)=inf{u>0:dim_R span_R(Lambda∩B_N(u))≥i}, for 1≤i≤R.

items.name: Gcd of maximal minors
items.statement: For independent c1,...,ck∈Z^N,1≤k≤N, G(c1,...,ck) is the positive gcd of all k×k minors of their column matrix.

items.name: Primitive lattices with prescribed minima
items.statement: For n≥2,1≤r≤n+1 and s_j≥1, S_{r,n}(s1,...,sr) is the set of primitive rank-r L⊂Z^{n+1} with s_j/2<lambda_j(L)≤s_j for every j.

items.name: One-band intrinsic section volume
items.statement: For independent w,z∈R^N, I(w,z)=vol_{N−1}{t∈(Rw)^perp:|<z,t>|≤||t||≤1}. Set delta(w,z)=||w||²||z||²−<w,z>²>0.

items.name: Primitive and unrestricted weighted lattice sums
items.statement: For integral Lambda⊂Z^N, bounded region R and integer k≥0, S_k*(Lambda;R)=sum_{a∈Lambda∩Z_prim^N∩R}||a||^{−k}; S_k(Lambda;R)=sum_{a∈(Lambda\{0})∩R}||a||^{−k}.

items.name: Definition 7.1 and Lemmas 7.2–7.3: local genus characters χ_Δ
items.statement: For a fundamental discriminant Δ and λ = [[b/2, −a], [c, −b/2]] ∈ L′_p with 4Q(λ) ∈ ΔZ_p, χ_{Δ,p}(λ) = (n, Δ)_p if gcd(a, b, c, Δ) = 1 and [a, b, c] represents n with (Δ, n) = 1, and 0 otherwise; χ_Δ = ∏_p χ_{Δ,p}. Lemma 7.2: χ_{Δ,p} is well defined and for p | Δ equals (a, Δ)_p if p ∤ a, (c, Δ)_p if p ∤ c, and 0 otherwise; on L it is the classical genus character (Gross–Kohnen–Zagier I.2). Lemma 7.3: χ_{Δ,p}(h·λ) = (det h, Δ)_p χ_{Δ,p}(λ) for h ∈ GL_2(Z_p).

items.name: Rank-three lattice Λ₂d
items.statement: For d>0 define Λ₂d=⟨2d⟩⊕U, with U the even unimodular hyperbolic plane. Its discriminant group is Z/(2d), with full-norm value 1/(2d) on the standard generator.

items.name: Primitive embedding data with complement identification
items.statement: For an even lattice S of signature(s₊,s₋) and target genus(m₊,m₋,q), take H_S⊂A_S,H_q⊂A_q, an isometry γ of restricted forms, δ=(q_S⊕−q)|Γ_γ^⊥/Γ_γ, an even K of signature(m₊−s₊,m₋−s₋), and an isometry γ_K:q_K→−δ. Primitive embeddings are classified up to target isometry by these data modulo target-discriminant isometries and compatible complement isometries. Passing to sublattice orbits additionally permits source isometries.

items.name: Regular quadratic forms and discriminants over rings
items.statement: For R a commutative ring and V a projective R-module of constant rank n with a quadratic form q, q is non-degenerate if β_q(x, y) = q(x + y) − q(x) − q(y) is a perfect pairing, and regular if it is non-degenerate or n is odd and Zariski-locally the half-discriminant is invertible ([Knu91, IV §3], 'semi-regular'). For V free and q non-degenerate, disc(q) ∈ R^×/R^{×2} is the class of the determinant of a Gram matrix of β_q.

items.name: GSpin, Spin and the spinor norm over rings
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and (V, q) regular over R: GSpin(V, q) is the group of even invertible elements of the Clifford algebra C(V, q) stabilising V under conjugation, with π: GSpin(V, q) → SO(V, q) of kernel the central GL_1 and Clifford norm ν: GSpin → GL_1 (ν(t) = t² on GL_1); Spin(V, q) = ker ν. There are exact sequences 1 → GL_1 → GSpin(V, q) → SO(V, q) → 1 of Zariski sheaves (3.2.1) and 1 → μ_2 → Spin(V, q) → SO(V, q) → 1 of fppf sheaves; the latter gives the spinor norm sn: SO(V, q)(R) → H¹_fppf(R, μ_2) ≃ R^×/R^{×2} when Pic R = 1, represented by ν(γ̃) for any lift γ̃ ∈ GSpin(V, q)(R). The spinor norm is multiplicative on orthogonal sums.

items.name: The finite sets X_n
items.statement: For n ≡ 0 mod 8, L_n is the set of even unimodular lattices in the standard Euclidean space R^n and X_n = O(R^n)\L_n the finite set of their isometry classes.

items.name: Siegel theta series
items.statement: For g ≥ 0, Siegel theta series give linear maps ϑ_g: C[X_n] → M_{n/2}(Γ_g) (5.3.1).

items.name: Least totally positive unit
items.statement: For a real quadratic field with its embedding √D>0, choose the least unit ε_D>1 of norm +1. Prove every positive norm-one unit is an integral power of ε_D. For D≡1 mod4 this uses the full ring of integers, not only Z[√D].

items.name: Minus continued fractions
items.statement: A minus expansion uses n₀−1/(n₁−1/(...)), with integral n₀ and n_j≥2 for j≥1. A primitive periodic cycle (n₁,...,n_ℓ), not all 2, is considered up to cyclic rotation; ℓ is the least period, and m=Σn_j.

items.name: Reduced real quadratic irrational
items.statement: For a real quadratic field with conjugation σ, w is reduced when 0<w^σ<1<w. Associate to a reduced primitive cycle its attracting real fixed point and its conjugate.

items.name: Integral binary quadratic forms
items.statement: For integers a,b,c, Q(x,y)=ax²+bxy+cy² has discriminant b²−4ac. Use proper SL₂(Z) equivalence; primitiveness means gcd(a,b,c)=1. For negative discriminant use positive definite forms; for positive nonsquare discriminant retain orientation, including both signs of Q.

items.name: Ideal to oriented form correspondence
items.statement: Normalize the norm form on an ideal representing A to obtain a primitive integral form Q=[a,b,c] of discriminant D. Under this correspondence A⁻¹, JA, JA⁻¹ correspond respectively to [a,−b,c], [−a,b,−c], [−a,−b,−c]. Include the scaling and basis conventions needed for well-defined proper equivalence.

items.name: Oriented axis and closed geodesic
items.statement: For reduced w representing A, orient the axis from w^σ to w, and quotient by the primitive γ_w with expanding eigenvalue ε_D. Its map to PSL₂(Z)\H is the parametrized closed geodesic C_A; retain its traversal multiplicity.

items.name: CM points and elliptic weights
items.statement: For negative discriminant D and a positive definite Q=[a,b,c], z_Q=(−b+i√|D|)/(2a). Pass to its modular class z_A and weight by 1/ω_Q, the order of its stabilizer in PSL₂(Z); for fundamental D, ω_D=3,2,1 at −3,−4,other D.

items.name: Genus Weyl functional
items.statement: For D=d′d nonsquare and χ its genus character, W(u,χ) is (λ/2)Σχ(A)∫_{F_A}u dμ when d,d′<0; Σχ(A)∫_{C_A}u ds when both positive; and ω_D^(−1)Σχ(A)u(z_A) when D<0. Here λ is the eigenvalue of u. These three normalizations differ from the extra 2√π used in Theorems3–4 for CM points.

items.name: Genus character on arbitrary discriminant forms
items.statement: For D=d′d nonsquare, d fundamental and d′ a discriminant, define χ_d([a,b,c])=0 if gcd(a,b,c,d)>1; otherwise take (d/m) for any represented m coprime to d. Positive definite forms are used if D<0; imprimitive forms are allowed.

items.name: Symplectic K-theory of Z
items.statement: SP(Z) is the symmetric monoidal groupoid of free Z-modules with a perfect skew-symmetric pairing under orthogonal sum; KSp(Z) := K(SP(Z)), KSp_i(Z; Z/q) := π_i(KSp(Z); Z/q), KSp_i(Z; Z_p) := lim_n KSp_i(Z; Z/p^n); equivalently KSp_i(Z; Z_p) = lim_g π_i(BSp_{2g}(Z)^∧_p) (§1.2), with the Hurewicz map KSp_i(Z; Z_p) → H_i(Sp_∞(Z); Z_p).

items.name: §2.3–2.4 (local representation densities and the normalized local Siegel series Den(T, L))
items.statement: For Hermitian O_{F′}-lattices M, L the representation density Den(M, L) is the limit of the normalized counts of representations mod ϖ^N; m(a; T) := Π_{i=0}^{a−1}(1 − (η(ϖ)q)^iT); for a torsion O_F-module T, ℓ(T) is its length and t(T) = dim_k(T ⊗ k), with ℓ′, t′ the O_{F′}-versions in the inert case and ℓ = 2ℓ′, t = 2t′; the type of a Hermitian lattice is t(L) = t(L^∨/L).

items.name: Definition 5.1, (5.1)–(5.5) (local densities, primitive local densities and their derivatives)
items.statement: For hermitian lattices M, L of ranks m, n: Den(M, L) = lim_d |Herm_{L,M}(O_{F_0}/π_0^{d+a})|/q^{2(d+a)nm−dn²}; Den(M, L, X) ∈ Q[X] with Den(M, L, q^{−2k}) = Den(M ⊥ H^k, L) (5.1), H the hyperbolic plane with matrix [[0, π^{−1}], [−π^{−1}, 0]]; Den′(M, L) = −2(d/dX)Den(M, L, X)|_{X=1} (5.2); the primitive version Pden(M, L, X) counting primitive ϕ (dim of the image of L in (M ⊥ H^k)/π(M ⊥ H^k) equal to n) (5.3); Pden′(L), Pden_t(L) (5.4) and ∂Pden(L) = Pden′(L) + Σ c_{2j}Pden_{2j}(L) (5.5). Den(M, L) = 0 for M, L of rank n with χ(M) = −χ(L) (Lemma 5.7). Normal bases and fundamental invariants follow [LL22, Def. 2.11, Lemma 2.12] (§1.5).

items.name: Admissible lattice-point exponents and the decomposition of D_small
items.statement: An exponent θ_l > 0 is admissible if there is C_l > 0 such that every ellipse defined by a definite integral binary quadratic form belongs to the class L(C_l, θ_l); van der Corput's bound makes every θ_l > 2/3 admissible and Huxley's bound every θ_l > 131/208. For m ∈ Z/k and i ∈ {0,1,2} put D_i(m) = ∏_{p | D_small, ord_p m = i} p, so that D_small = D_0(m)D_1(m)D_2(m).
