items.name: Definition 2.14 (local densities over a ramified extension)
items.statement: Den(M, L) = lim_N #Herm_{L,M}(O_F/(u^{2N}))/q^{N·d_{L,M}}, d_{L,M} = dim Herm_{L,M} ⊗ F; H is the hyperbolic plane with matrix [[0, u^{−1}], [−u^{−1}, 0]] and H_s = H^{⊕s}, self-dual of rank 2s.

items.name: Definition 2.16 and Remark 2.17 (normalized local Siegel series, ramified case)
items.statement: For an O_E-lattice 𝐋 of the nonsplit 𝐕 of dimension n = 2r: Den(X, 𝐋) ∈ Z[X] with Den(q^{−s}, 𝐋) = Den(H_{r+s}, 𝐋)/Π_{i=s+1}^{r+s}(1 − q^{−2i}) for s ≥ 0; ∂Den(𝐋) = −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den(X, 𝐋); Den(1, 𝐋) = Den(H_r, 𝐋) = 0 since 𝐕 is nonsplit.

items.name: Hermitian spaces and lattices over an unramified quadratic extension
items.statement: F/F_0 unramified quadratic, residue field k = F_q. Hermitian spaces are classified by dimension and disc(V) = (−1)^{n(n−1)/2} det(V) ∈ F_0^×/Nm F^× [Jac62, Thm. 3.1]; V is split if disc = 1 and nonsplit otherwise. For an integral O_F-lattice L (L ⊆ L^∨): fundamental invariants 0 ≤ a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_n with L^∨/L ≅ ⊕ O_F/ϖ^{a_i}, val(L) = Σ a_i, type t(L) = #{a_i > 0}; vertex (minuscule) lattices L ⊆ L^∨ ⊆ ϖ^{−1}L, Vert^t the vertex lattices of type t; self-dual = type 0, almost self-dual = type 1. If V is split, val(L) is even and V contains a self-dual lattice; if nonsplit, val(L) is odd and V contains an almost self-dual lattice.

items.name: Local densities of hermitian lattices
items.statement: For hermitian O_F-lattices L (rank n) and M (rank m), Rep_{M,L}(R) = Herm(L ⊗ R, M ⊗ R) and Den(M, L) = lim_N #Rep_{M,L}(O_{F_0}/ϖ^N)/q^{N·dim(Rep_{M,L})_{F_0}}. If (Rep_{M,L})_{F_0} ≠ ∅ then n ≤ m and dim = dim U_m − dim U_{m−n} = n(2m − n) (3.1.0.2).

items.name: The normalized local Siegel series Den(X, L) and its central derivative
items.statement: Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L) is a polynomial in (−q)^{−k} with Q-coefficients [Hir98, Thm. II], and Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, ⟨1⟩^n) = Π_{i=1}^{n}(1 − (−q)^{−i}X)|_{X=(−q)^{−k}} (3.2.0.1). Den(X, L) ∈ Z[X] is the polynomial with Den((−q)^{−k}, L) = Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, L)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n+k}, ⟨1⟩^n). Den(L) := Den(1, L), and when val(L) is odd, ∂Den(L) := −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den(X, L). Both depend only on the fundamental invariants.

items.name: Lattice notation for L^♭: (L^♭)^{∨,∘}, e_max and M(L^♭)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ of rank n − 1 with L^♭_F nondegenerate: (L^♭)^{∨,∘} = {x ∈ (L^♭)^∨ : (x, x) ∈ O_F}; e_max(L^♭) = a_{n−1}; M(L^♭) = L^♭ ⊕ ⟨u⟩ with u ⊥ L^♭ of valuation a_{n−1} or a_{n−1} + 1 (⟨u⟩ = {x ⊥ L^♭ : val(x) ≥ a_{n−1}}), with invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−1}, a_{n−1}) or (…, a_{n−1} + 1). If L^♭ ⊆ L′^♭ then e_max(L′^♭) ≤ e_max(L^♭) and M(L^♭) ⊆ M(L′^♭) (7.1.0.4).

items.name: Definition 9.1.4 (Siegel series relative to Λ)
items.statement: Den_Λ(X, L) ∈ Z[X] with Den_Λ((−q)^{−k}, L) = Den(Λ ⊕ ⟨1⟩^k, L)/Den(⟨1⟩^{n−1} ⊕ ⟨1⟩^k, ⟨1⟩^{n−1}); by Theorem 9.1.2 Den_Λ(X, L) = Den(X, L^♯) (9.1.4.2). If val(L) is even, Den_Λ(1, L) = 0 and ∂Den_Λ(L) := −(d/dX)|_{X=1} Den_Λ(X, L).

items.name: Quadratic lattices and spaces over a p-adic field (§2.1)
items.statement: For a non-degenerate quadratic O_F-lattice L: L^∨, integrality, fundamental invariants (a_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ a_n) with L^∨/L ≅ ⊕ O_F/ϖ^{a_i}, val(L) = Σa_i, type t(L), standard orthogonal bases, self-dual and vertex (minuscule) lattices (L ⊆_t L^∨ ⊆ ϖ^{−1}L), det, disc(L) = (−1)^{C(n,2)}det(L), χ(L) = χ(disc L) ∈ {±1, 0}, Hasse invariant ϵ(W) = Π_{i<j}(u_i, u_j)_F, the classification of quadratic spaces by (dim, disc, ϵ) with the excluded cases in dimensions 1 and 2, W^{≥k}, W^{=k}, W° (integral cone), W°° (positive cone), W^an, Vert^t(W), H^ε_m (self-dual, χ = ε) and V^ε_m (χ = ε, ϵ = −1).

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 (local density of integral representations)
items.statement: Rep_{M,L}(R) = QHom(L ⊗ R, M ⊗ R), Den(M, L) = lim_N #Rep_{M,L}(O_F/ϖ^N)/q^{N·dim(Rep_{M,L})_F}, with dim(Rep_{M,L})_F = n(2m − n − 1)/2 (3.1.1.2).

items.name: Definitions 3.8.1–3.8.2, Corollary 3.8.3 and Lemma 3.8.4 (horizontal lattices)
items.statement: L^♭ ⊆ V^ε_m of rank n − 1 is co-isotropic iff (L^♭_F)^⊥ is isotropic iff χ(L^♭) = ε, and horizontal if integral with t(L^♭) ≤ 1, or t(L^♭) = 2 and ε sgn_{n−1}(L^♭) = +1; Hor^ε(L^♭) = {horizontal M^♭ ⊇ L^♭}. Corollary 3.8.3: co-isotropic L^♭ has Den^♭ε(1, L^♭) = 0 and Hor^ε(L^♭) = ∅; for co-anisotropic L^♭, ∂Den^ε(L) − ∂Den^ε(L̃) = Σ_{M^♭ ∈ Hor^ε(L^♭)} q^{⌊val(M^♭)/2⌋}·(1, (1 + q^{−1}), 2(1 + q^{−1})) by type (χ(L^♭) ≠ 0), with the analogous formula for χ(L^♭) = 0. Lemma 3.8.4: a rank n − 1 lattice embedding in V^ε_m and H^ε_m with M^♭ = M^♭_F ∩ H^ε_m is horizontal.

items.name: Local monogenic order
items.statement: For a monic irreducible f∈Z_ℓ[X] with separable fraction algebra F, R=Z_ℓ[X]/(f)⊂O_F; an R-lattice of rank n is a full Z_ℓ-lattice in F^n stable under R.

items.name: Stable lattice with prescribed flag quotients
items.statement: For semisimple γ preserving 0⊂V₁⊂V and V₂=V/V₁, fix full γ-stable lattices U₁⊂V₁,U₂⊂V₂. Consider full γ-stable L⊂V with L∩V₁=U₁ and image U₂.

items.name: Finite-colength ideal count
items.statement: For a complete DVR O with residue field F_q, Hilb^j_(O[[X]]) denotes ideals I with O-module length(O[[X]]/I)=j.

items.name: Model ring with positive involution
items.statement: For distinct CM fields L_i with real subfields K_i and n_i>0 satisfying Σ_i n_i[L_i:Q]=2g, R_(L,n)=∏_i M_(n_i)(O_(L_i)) with conjugate-transpose involution.

items.name: Positive-unit model orbit count
items.statement: n_(L,n) is the number of R_(L,n)^×-orbits on positive self-adjoint units by a↦g*ag.

items.name: Totally positive unit norm labels
items.statement: Σ=O_K^(×,+)/N_(L/K)(O_L^×), with chosen representatives ε_σ; on L^n set h_σ(z,w)=ε_σ z₁ conjugate(w₁)+Σ_(i>1) z_i conjugate(w_i).

items.name: Unitary group of a definite hermitian space
items.statement: U_σ is the K-algebraic group preserving h_σ; its K-points act on O_L-lattices by isometries.

items.name: Integral projective hermitian lattice
items.statement: An O_L-lattice M in L^n is finitely generated, full and locally free of rank n, and integral when h(M,M)⊂O_L. Free lattices form a distinguished subclass.

items.name: Dual and unimodularity
items.statement: M∨={x∈L^n:h(x,M)⊂O_L}; an integral hermitian lattice is unimodular if M=M∨.

items.name: Norm ideal of a local hermitian lattice
items.statement: n(M) is the O_(L_v)-ideal generated by h(m,m), m∈M, for a lattice in a fixed localized hermitian space.

items.name: Genus of a hermitian lattice
items.statement: The genus of M comprises projective unimodular lattices in its rational hermitian space locally isometric to M at every finite place, modulo global isometry.

items.name: Weighted hermitian genus mass
items.statement: mass(C)=Σ_[M]∈C 1/|Aut(M)| for a positive definite hermitian genus with finitely many isometry classes.

items.name: Local representation densities of a quadratic lattice
items.statement: For a quadratic Z-lattice (L,Q), det(L) is the determinant of its Gram matrix, and for a rational prime ℓ the local density is δ(ℓ,L,m) = lim_{a→∞} ℓ^{a(1-rk L)}#{v ∈ L/ℓ^a L : Q(v) ≡ m mod ℓ^a}. If m is represented by (L ⊗ Z_ℓ, Q) then δ(ℓ,L,m) > 0; moreover for rk L ≥ 5 and a fixed ℓ one has δ(ℓ,L,m) ≍ 1 for every m represented over Z_ℓ.

items.name: Successive minima of the lattices L_n
items.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ r = rk_Z L_n, the i-th successive minimum μ_i(n) of L_n is inf{y > 0 : there are linearly independent v_1,…,v_i ∈ L_n with Q(v_j) ≤ y^2}; set a_i(n) = ∏_{j≤i}μ_j(n) and a_0(n) = 1.

items.name: Local counts N_m(p^n), densities μ_p(m, n) and w_p(m)
items.statement: N_m(p^n) = #{v ∈ L/p^nL : Q(v) ≡ m mod p^n}, μ_p(m, n) = p^{−n(r−1)} N_m(p^n) (4.1); w_p(m) = 1 + val_p(m) for p ≠ 2 and w_2(m) = 1 + 2val_2(2m). The local density is μ_p(Q, m) = lim_k μ_p(m, k), which stabilizes for k ≫ 1.

items.name: Jordan splitting of a maximal L_p and Hanke's solution types
items.statement: (L_p, Q) = ⊕_j (L_j, p^{ν_j}Q_j) with (L_j, Q_j) unimodular of rank 1 or 2 (rank 1 if p ≠ 2) [Han04, (2.3), Lemma 2.1]; maximality of L_p forces ν_j ≤ 1. S_i = {j : ν_j = i}, s_i = #S_i. A solution v ∈ N_m(p^n) is of zero type if v ≡ 0 mod p, of good type if v_j ≢ 0 mod p for some j with ν_j = 0, and of bad type otherwise; μ^good, μ^bad, μ^zero are the corresponding densities; Q′ replaces each ν_j by 1 − ν_j. N_m = N_m^good when p ∤ m; N_m^zero(p^n) = ∅ when p² ∤ m and n ≥ 2; N_m^bad = ∅ when p ∤ 2det(L) [Han04, Def. 3.1, Rem. 3.4.1].

items.name: Successive minima (Definition 7.4)
items.statement: For a lattice L_n of rank r with positive definite Q and 1 ≤ i ≤ r: μ_i(n) = inf{y > 0 : there are linearly independent v_1, …, v_i ∈ L_n with Q(v_j) ≤ y²}; a_i(n) = Π_{j≤i} μ_j(n), a_0(n) = 1 [EK95].

items.name: Hermitian-to-quadratic convention
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero quadratic extension F/F0, an F/F0-Hermitian form is linear in its first argument. Its F0-quadratic form is q(u)=h(u,u); its associated bilinear form is TrF/F0 h and has diagonal 2q. Norm fibres are Vξ={u:q(u)=ξ}.

items.name: Maximal orders in B and the compact subgroups K_v
items.statement: Fix a maximal Z-order O ⊂ B(Q). For finite v its v-adic closure O_v is a maximal Z_v-order of B(Q_v), and K_v < G(Q_v) is the image of O_v^×; G(A) and B^×(A) are restricted products with respect to the K_v and O_v. If B splits at a finite v, the maximal orders of B(Q_v) ≅ End_{Q_v}(Q_v^2) are the End_{Z_v}(L) for full-rank Z_v-lattices L, in bijection with the vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree; O_v^× is a vertex stabiliser and K_v is a special maximal compact-open subgroup. If B ramifies at a finite v, O_v is the unique maximal order (the integral closure of Z_v), O_v^× is normal in B^×(Q_v), and K_v is normal of index 2 in the compact group G(Q_v). At ∞ fix a maximal compact torus K_∞ < G(R). If B(R) is split, fix an algebra isomorphism B(R) ≅ M_2(R) carrying K_∞ to PSO_2(R) (unique up to Ad PGO_2(R)) and let ‖·‖_∞ be the operator norm of the Euclidean norm on R^2, which does not depend on that choice; if B(R) is the Hamilton quaternions, ‖·‖_∞ = √Nrd. Then ‖g^{-1}‖_∞ = ‖g‖_∞/|Nrd g| for g ∈ B^×(R). Set O_∞ = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g‖_∞ ≤ 1}, O_∞^× = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g‖_∞ = 1, Nrd g = 1} (in the split case the orientation-preserving isotropy group of |·|_∞, ≅ SO_2(R)), and Ω̃_∞ = {g ∈ B^×(R) : ‖g^{±1}‖_∞ ≤ 2, Nrd g > 0}, a connected, symmetric, compact identity neighbourhood with O_∞^×Ω̃_∞ = Ω̃_∞O_∞^× = Ω̃_∞ on which 1/4 ≤ Nrd g ≤ 4.

items.name: Homogeneous toral sets and toral packets
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q and g ∈ G(A), the set [T(A)g] ⊂ [G(A)] is a homogeneous toral set. It is a right translate of [T(A)] ≅ T(Q)\T(A) and carries a unique probability measure invariant under the right action of H_A := g^{-1}T(A)g, the periodic toral measure. A toral packet P is a finite collection of orbits in Ỹ of a real torus H < G(R) that is the projection of a single adelic torus orbit. The set of H-orbits in P is a principal homogeneous space for a finite abelian group C, a quotient of the idele class group of the attached quadratic field E/Q, and there is a canonical surjection C → Pic(Λ), which is an isomorphism when K_f is maximal.

items.name: Joinings of periodic toral measures
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G anisotropic over Q, s ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A), the set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] ⊂ [(G × G)(A)] is a joint homogeneous toral set, a homogeneous set for the non-maximal rank-one anisotropic torus T^Δ. It carries a probability measure μ^joint invariant under the right action of H_A^Δ, where H_A = g^{-1}T(A)g. Each coordinate projection of μ^joint is the periodic toral measure on [T(A)g], so μ^joint is a self-joining of it, the self-joining with twist s. The whole class of s in T(Q)\T(A) gives the same joining.

items.name: n-fold joint homogeneous toral sets
items.statement: Fix n ∈ N, a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q, its diagonal T^Δ < G^{×n}, elements s_1, …, s_{n−1} ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A). The set [T^Δ(A)(g, s_1g, …, s_{n−1}g)] ⊂ [G^{×n}(A)] is an n-joint homogeneous toral set.

items.name: Algebraic measures on adelic quotients
items.statement: Let M be a linear algebraic group over Q. (1) Fix a finite set S of places containing ∞, a closed finite-index subgroup M < M(Q_S) and a lattice Γ < M. A probability measure ν on Γ\M is algebraic if there are a closed unimodular algebraic subgroup L < M defined and anisotropic over Q, a finite-index subgroup L < L(Q_S) and g_S ∈ M such that ν is the L-Haar probability measure on [Lg_S] ⊆ Γ\M. (2) A probability measure ν on [M(A)] is algebraic if there are a closed unimodular algebraic Q-subgroup L < M anisotropic over Q, a Q-isogeny L' → L and a closed finite-index subgroup L < Im[L'(A) → L(A)] such that ν is the L-Haar probability measure on an orbit [Lg] ⊂ [M(A)], g ∈ M(A). The datum is the M(Q)-orbit of (L, L' → L, L, Lg), with γ acting by conjugation and left translation.

items.name: The split tori A_{p_i} and their positive parts
items.statement: For i ∈ {1, 2}, A_{p_i} < G(Q_{p_i}) is the maximal split torus fixed once and for all in §2.4.1, with A_{p_1} ∩ K_{p_1} maximal compact in A_{p_1}; every homogeneous toral set considered satisfies g_{p_i}^{-1}T(Q_{p_i})g_{p_i} = A_{p_i} by (♠). Put A_{p_i}^+ := A_{p_i} ∩ G(Q_{p_i})^+, the image in A_{p_i} of a maximal torus of G^sc(Q_{p_i}) isogenous to A_{p_i}; it has finite index in A_{p_i}.

items.name: Coordinates for a quaternion algebra split by E
items.statement: M_{2×2} = Spec Q[x_{i,j} : 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 2]. GL_2 is the closed subscheme of M_{2×2} × A^1 with Q[GL_2] = Q[x_{i,j}, det^{-1}]/⟨(x_{1,1}x_{2,2} − x_{1,2}x_{2,1})det^{-1} = 1⟩. Let Ã < GL_2 be the diagonal torus. Since T̃ ≅ Res_{E/Q}G_m splits over E, fix an E-algebra isomorphism B_E → M_{2×2,E} carrying T̃_E to Ã_E, and identify B_E = M_{2×2,E}, B_E^× = GL_{2,E}, T̃_E = Ã_E, G_E = PGL_{2,E}, T_E = A_E. With 𝔊 = Gal(E/Q) = {1, σ}, the naive action of σ is x_{i,j} ↦ ^σx_{i,j}, and the twisted action giving the Q-form B is x ↦ θ·^σx·θ^{-1} for some θ ∈ PGL_2(E). The two actions differ even when B = M_{2×2}.

items.name: Denominators and good integral representatives
items.statement: (1) For finite v where G splits, ℬ_v is the Bruhat–Tits tree of G(Q_v); for finite v where G ramifies, ℬ_v is the connected graph with two vertices G(Q_v)/K_v; d is the path metric with edges of length 1. (2) If B(R) is split, ℬ_∞ = G(R)/N_{G(R)}(K_∞), the upper half-plane with the standard hyperbolic distance d; if B(R) is ramified, ℬ_∞ is a point. (3) For each place v let x_0 ∈ ℬ_v be the point fixed by K_v, let q be the residue characteristic if v ≠ ∞ and q = e if v = ∞, and define the continuous function 𝔡_v : G(Q_v) → R_{>0} (arXiv: Denom_v) by 𝔡_v(x_v) := q^{d(x_0, x_v.x_0)}. (4) 𝔡_f : G(A_f) → N is the continuous function 𝔡_f((x_v)_{v≠∞}) := ∏_{v≠∞} 𝔡_v(x_v).

items.name: Bowen balls for the diagonal flow
items.statement: Let B ⊆ G(Q_{p_1}) be an identity neighbourhood, λ a cocharacter spanning X_•(A_{p_1}) and a = λ(p_1). The symmetric homogeneous B-Bowen ball is B^{(−n,n)} = ∩_{k=−n}^{n} a^kBa^{-k}.

items.name: The GIT double quotient W
items.statement: Let M = G × T act on the affine variety G × G, the G-coordinate by diagonal left multiplication and the T-coordinate by diagonal right multiplication by the inverse; W denotes the GIT quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ. Let w_T ∈ N_G T(Q) be a rational representative of the nontrivial Weyl class; the variety w_TT is well defined even though w_T is not.

items.name: The simply connected torus T^{(1)}
items.statement: G^sc is the group of unit quaternions in B; T^{(1)} is the maximal torus of G^sc over Q mapping to T under the isogeny, namely the unit quaternions in T̃. Likewise A^{(1)} < GL_2 is the rank-one torus of diagonal matrices of determinant 1 and A the split diagonal torus of PGL_2, with A^{(1)} → A surjective as schemes.

items.name: The invariant functions ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ
items.statement: Let A^{(1)} act on M_{2×2} × A^1 by conjugating the matrix and fixing the det^{-1} coordinate; this is equivariant for GL_2 ↪ M_{2×2} × A^1. Define ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ ∈ Q[M_{2×2}] to be, respectively, the two diagonal entries and the product of the off-diagonal entries.

items.name: Homogeneous Hecke sets
items.statement: For ξ = (ξ_1, ξ_2) ∈ (G × G)(A), [G^Δ(A)ξ] is a homogeneous Hecke set; it carries a ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)ξ-invariant algebraic probability measure. [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] is a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set; it carries a ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)^+ξ-invariant algebraic probability measure. With G^Δ fixed, [G^Δ(A)ξ] is determined by the coset G^Δ(A)ξ ∈ G^Δ(A)\(G × G)(A), identified through the contraction map with ctr(ξ) ∈ G(A). [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] is determined by G^Δ(A)^+ξ ∈ G^Δ(A)^+\(G × G)(A), identified with the pair ([ξ_1] ∈ G(A)/G(A)^+, ctr(ξ) ∈ G(A)).

items.name: The split-place denominator
items.statement: Define the proper continuous function Denom_sf : G(A_f) → N by Denom_sf(h_f) = ∏_{v ≠ ∞ splitting B} Denom_v(h_v); since 1 ≤ Denom_v(ξ_v) ≤ q_v at the finitely many ramified places, Denom_sf ≍_G Denom_f on G(A_f).

items.name: The automorphic kernel and the pair cross-correlation
items.statement: For a compact identity neighbourhood V ⊆ [(G×G)(A)], the automorphic kernel K_V : [(G×G)(A)]^{×2} → R is K_V(x,y) = Σ_{γ∈(G×G)(Q)} 1_V(x^{-1}γy). The sum is finite, and the number of non-zero terms is bounded uniformly for x, y in fixed compact sets. Let B = ∏_v B_v ⊆ G(A) be a compact identity neighbourhood with B_v = K_v for almost all v and B_v a compact-open subgroup for every non-archimedean v. Let λ_1, λ_2 be probability measures on [(G×G)(A)] and C ⊆ [G(A)] closed. Define Cor_C[λ_1,λ_2](B) := ∫_{C×C}∫_{C×C} K_{B×B}(x,y) dλ_1(x) dλ_2(y), and Cor[λ_1,λ_2](B) := Cor_{Y_A}[λ_1,λ_2](B). B is injective on C if the quotient map G(A) → [G(A)] is injective on gB for every g with [g] ∈ C; for compact C such an identity neighbourhood exists. Then λ_1×λ_2({(x,y) ∈ (C×C)×(C×C) : y ∈ x(B×B)}) ≤ Cor_C[λ_1,λ_2](B), with equality if B is injective on C.

items.name: The ideals attached to a joint toral set
items.statement: Fix a joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g,sg)] with global order Λ. (1) The twist s ∈ T(A) defines the homothety class Q^×𝔰 := idl(s) ∈ Q^×\𝒥(Λ) of invertible fractional Λ-ideals. (2) 𝔢 := idl~((υ_vτ_v)_v), where υ_v, τ_v are the local elements of Proposition 5.19 in the coordinates of the local maximal orders. It is an invertible fractional Λ-ideal recording the splitting of B outside ∞. (3) υ := sign(ε)·∏_{p : B is ramified at p and E is inert at p} p ∈ Z. When G ≃ PGL_2 is split, one may take ε = 1, and then υ = 1 and 𝔢 = Λ.

items.name: The counting functions f_{[𝔤]} and g_{[𝔤]}
items.statement: For [𝔤] ∈ Pic(Λ) define f_{[𝔤]}, g_{[𝔤]} : Z → Z by g_{[𝔤]}(x) = #{𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ)_0 : Nr 𝔞 = x, 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, and [𝔞] = [𝔤] or 𝔞 = 0} and f_{[𝔤]}(x) = #{𝔟 ∈ 𝒥(Λ) : Nr 𝔟 = x, 𝔟 ⊆ Λ, [𝔟] ∈ [𝔤]Pic(Λ)²}, where 𝒥(Λ)_0 = 𝒥(Λ) ∪ {0·Λ}. Let r : N → N be the multiplicative function defined by the following values, for k ≥ 1. For an odd prime p | D at which B splits, r(p^k) = 1 if k < ord_p D and r(p^k) = 2 if k ≥ ord_p D. If 2 | D, r(2^k) = 2^{μ_wild}, with μ_wild = ord_2[Z_2^× : Nr Λ_2^×] as in Corollary A.7. If p | D and B ramifies at p, r(p^k) = 2. For p ∤ D, r(p^k) = 1.

items.name: The rational double quotient W_Q and the dagger subgroups
items.statement: Set W_Q = G^Δ(Q)\(G × G)(Q)/T^Δ(Q), with a natural map to W(Q). For a closed subgroup N < M(A) write N^† = N ∩ (G(A)^+ × T(A)), always normal in N.

items.name: Relative orbital integrals
items.statement: Fix γ ∈ (G×G)(Q) with M_γ(A) compact, so that M_γ(Q) is finite. With the Haar measure of M_γ(A)^† normalised to mass 1, RO_{γ,κ}(B) = ∫_{M(A)^†} 1_{B′}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t), and Σ_{κ∈π_G(M_γ(Q))\G(Q)/G(Q)^+} vol(M_γ)·RO_{γ,κ}(B) = (#M_γ(Q))^{-1}·Σ_{κ∈G(Q)/G(Q)^+} RO_{γ,κ}(B). For κ ∈ G(Q), RO_{γ,κ}(B) = RO^∞_{γ,κ}(B)·RO^f_{γ,κ}(B), where RO^∞_{γ,κ}(B) := ∫_{M(R)^†} 1_{B′_∞}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t) and RO^f_{γ,κ}(B) := ∫_{M(A_f)^†} 1_{B′_f}((κl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t).

items.name: The invariant map inv
items.statement: Let K_{T,f} := T(A_f) ∩ g_fK_fg_f^{-1}. Define inv_f : Ad K_{T,f}\G(A_f) → Q^×_Δ\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)_0) as follows. For v ≠ ∞, write a representative of h_v in B^×(Q_v) in the coordinates of Proposition 5.19 as h_v = Q_v^×·(α_v, β_vυ_vτ_v ; ^σβ_v/τ_v, ^σα_v) with α_v, β_v ∈ E_v. Set inv_f([h_f]) := (idl~(α_v), idl~(β_v)) = (∩_{v≠∞} α_vΛ_v, ∩_{v≠∞} β_vΛ_v). The pair is well defined up to multiplying both entries by one element of Q^×, since Q has class number one. It is invariant under conjugation by K_{T,f}, which multiplies β_v by an element of cbd(Λ_v^×) ⊂ Λ_v^×. Put G(A)_accessible := Ad T(A)G(Q), an Ad T(A)-invariant subset of G(A). Define inv : Ad T(R)Ad K_{T,f}\G(A)_accessible → Q^×\(𝒥(Λ)_0 × 𝒥(Λ)_0) by applying inv_f to the finite part. On accessible elements the local maps π_W : Ad T(Q_v)\G(Q_v) → W(Q_v) take a common value in W(Q) at every place; this defines π_W : Ad T(A)\G(A)_accessible → W(Q).

items.name: The ideal-counting multiplicative functions
items.statement: Let f : N → N be f(n) := #{𝔞 ∈ 𝒥(Λ) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, Nr 𝔞 = n}, the multiplicative count of integral invertible Λ-ideals of norm n. Let r_0 : N → Z be the multiplicative function with r_0(p^k) = 2 if p | D_large and k ≥ ord_p D, and r_0(p^k) = 1 otherwise. Here D = D_small·D_large is the splitting of §10.2; see the proposed new item on D_small.

items.name: Local invariance groups for the orbital integrals
items.statement: Let B_f < G(A_f) be a compact-open subgroup, and fix a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+(ξ_1,ξ_2)] and a homogeneous toral set [T(A)g]. Put B_{G,f} := ξ_{1,f}B_fξ_{1,f}^{-1} ∩ ξ_{2,f}B_fξ_{2,f}^{-1} < G(A_f), B^+_{G,f} := B_{G,f} ∩ G(A_f)^+, B_{T,f} := g_fB_fg_f^{-1} ∩ T(A_f), B_{M,f} := B_{G,f} × B_{T,f} < M(A_f) and B^†_{M,f} := B^+_{G,f} × B_{T,f} < M(A_f)^†. Each is a compact-open subgroup of its group. For γ ∈ (G×G)(Q) and κ ∈ G(Q), put f_{γ,κ}(l,t) := 1_{B′_f}((κl)^{-1}γt) and f_γ(l,t) := 1_{B′_f}(l^{-1}γt). Then f_{γ,κ} is B^†_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f)^†, and f_γ is B_{M,f}-invariant on M(A_f).

items.name: Special places and the standing normalisation (♠)
items.statement: Fix once and for all two finite primes p_1, p_2 at which G splits, maximal split tori A_{p_1} < G(Q_{p_1}) and A_{p_2} < G(Q_{p_2}) such that A_{p_1} ∩ K_{p_1} is maximal compact in A_{p_1} (equivalently, the apartment of A_{p_1} in the Bruhat–Tits tree contains the vertex fixed by K_{p_1}), and the maximal compact torus K_∞ < G(R) of §2.2.1. A homogeneous toral set [T(A)g], with T split at p_1 and p_2 and anisotropic at ∞, satisfies (♠) if g_∞^{-1}T(R)g_∞ = K_∞, g_{p_1}^{-1}T(Q_{p_1})g_{p_1} = A_{p_1} and g_{p_2}^{-1}T(Q_{p_2})g_{p_2} = A_{p_2}. A joint set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] satisfies (♠) if [T(A)g] does. Under (♠) the splitting field E of T is imaginary quadratic and split at p_1 and p_2, and the local discriminants D_∞, D_{p_1}, D_{p_2} are the same for all such sets.

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: Fix a compact identity neighbourhood Ω = ∏_vΩ_v ⊂ G(A). For a homogeneous toral set [T(A)g], normalise the Haar measure on H_A = g^{-1}T(A)g so that H_A ∩ Ω has mass 1; vol([T(A)g]) is the total mass of [T(A)g] for the induced measure, equivalently vol([T(A)g]) = m_T(T(A) ∩ gΩg^{-1})^{-1} with m_T the covolume-one Haar measure on T(A). For compact identity neighbourhoods Ω, Ω', vol_Ω ≪_{Ω,Ω'} vol_{Ω'} ≪_{Ω,Ω'} vol_Ω, with constants independent of the toral set. The paper fixes Ω_v = K_v for finite v and Ω_∞ = Z(R)Ω̃_∞, a connected, compact, symmetric, Ad K_∞-invariant identity neighbourhood that equals G(R) if B is ramified at ∞. With Ω × Ω and O × O as references on G × G, vol([T^Δ(A)(g, sg)]) = vol([T(A)g]) and disc([T^Δ(A)(g, sg)]) = disc([T(A)g]).

items.name: The coboundary map and Hilbert 90
items.statement: Let F be a quadratic extension of Q or of Q_v, or a quadratic étale Q_v-algebra, with 𝔊 ≅ Z/2Z acting and σ the non-trivial element. Let F^{(1)} be the group of norm-one elements of F^× and O_F^{(1)} its integral elements. The coboundary map cbd : F^× → F^{(1)}, x ↦ x/^σx, is a surjective homomorphism (Hilbert's Theorem 90; directly in the split case F = Q_v × Q_v).

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous Hecke set
items.statement: For ξ ∈ (G × G)(A), vol([G^Δ(A)ξ]) := m_{G^Δ}(G^Δ(A) ∩ ξ(Ω × Ω)ξ^{-1})^{-1} = m_G(Ω ∩ ctr(ξ)Ωctr(ξ)^{-1})^{-1}, where m_G = m_{G^Δ} is the covolume-one Haar measure and Ω is the fixed reference neighbourhood of §2.4.5. The volume of a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set is defined analogously. The map ξ ↦ vol([G^Δ(A)ξ]) is continuous from (G × G)(A) to R_{>0} and factors through ctr : (G × G)(A) → G(A).

items.name: The small part of the discriminant and the genus weights
items.statement: Fix C_θ ≥ 1 with C_θ^{-1}X ≤ Σ_{p≤X} log p ≤ C_θX for all X ∈ N (Chebyshev), and 1/2 > η > 0. Write D = D_small·D_large, where D_small := ∏_{p ∥ D, p ∤ ω, 2 < p ≤ (η/(4C_θ))·log|D|} p; then D_small ≤ |D|^{η/4}. Put k := υp_1^{2n}D_small², so that Z/kZ = Z/υZ × Z/p_1^{2n}Z × ∏_{p|D_small} Z/p²Z. For p | D_small, partition Z/p²Z = C_{+0} ⊔ C_{−0} ⊔ C_{+1} ⊔ C_{−1} ⊔ C_2, where C_{±0} := {u ∈ (Z/p²Z)^× : (u/p) = ±1}, C_{±1} := {pu : u ∈ (Z/pZ)^×, (u/p) = ±1} and C_2 := {0}. Let w_p be the measure on Z/p²Z that is uniform on each atom, with w_p(C_{±0}) = #C_{±0} = (p²/2)(1 − 1/p) and w_p(C_2) = 2. For ε ∈ {±1}, w_p(C_ε) = 2·#C_ε = p(1 − 1/p) if χ_p(Nr(p_1^n𝔰𝔢)) = −ε, and w_p(C_ε) = 0 otherwise. Set w_k := δ_{0 mod υ} × δ_{0 mod p_1^{2n}} × ∏_{p|D_small} w_p on Z/kZ. For m ∈ Z/kZ, D_i(m) := ∏_{p|D_small, ord_p m = i} p (Definition 10.9, item 95).

items.name: Quasitrivial torus
items.statement: A k-torus Q is quasitrivial if Q≅Res_E/k G_m for some finite étale k-algebra E, equivalently its character lattice is a permutation Γ_k-module.

items.name: Homogeneous space and geometric stabilizer
items.statement: A smooth geometrically integral k-variety V with action of a connected linear k-group G is homogeneous when G_kbar acts transitively; at a geometric point v, H is its group-scheme stabilizer. Arithmetic sections do not assume v is k-rational.

items.name: Outer Galois action on finite stabilizers
items.statement: For a homogeneous space under a semisimple simply connected G in characteristic zero with finite geometric stabilizer H, the fundamental exact sequence gives a continuous Γ_k→Out(H); changing the geometric basepoint changes only the inner identifications. H^ab inherits an honest Γ_k-action.

items.name: Type of a multiplicative-type torsor
items.statement: If V is smooth geometrically integral with kbar[V]^×=kbar^× and R is of multiplicative type, an R-torsor has type λ:R̂→Pic(V_kbar), sending a character to its associated line bundle; H¹(V_kbar,R_kbar)=Hom(R̂,Pic(V_kbar)).

items.name: Universal torsor
items.statement: When Pic(V_kbar) is finitely generated, a universal torsor on V is a torsor under the multiplicative-type group dual to Pic(V_kbar) whose type is the identity. Existence over k is a separate obstruction question.

items.name: Pullback character module and group extension
items.statement: Given λ:R̂→Pic(V_kbar), define T̂=R̂×_{Pic(V_kbar)}Pic(X_kbar), ν:T̂→Pic(X_kbar), and Q̂=Div_boundary(X_kbar). Then 0→Q̂→T̂→R̂→0 dualizes to 1→R→T→Q→1 with Q quasitrivial. T need not be a torus before torsion-freeness is checked.

items.name: Split fibre
items.statement: A finite-type scheme over a field is split in the fibration sense when it contains a geometrically integral open subscheme, equivalently in the generically reduced fibre situations used here it has a geometrically irreducible component of multiplicity one.

items.name: Quasitrivial-base compactified fibration
items.statement: Over a number field k take E finite étale of degree n, Q=Res_E/k G_m⊂Q_aff=Res_E/k A¹≅A^n⊂P^n, and a dominant f:X→P^n with X smooth proper irreducible and geometrically rationally connected generic fibre.

items.name: Norm base changes indexed by Q(k)
items.statement: Choose a finite extension ℓ/k splitting the finitely many boundary fibres. Put Q′=Res_(E⊗ℓ)/k G_m and define b_aff(r):Q′_aff→Q_aff by z↦rN_(E⊗ℓ)/E(z), r∈Q(k). Pull back the smooth open V=f⁻¹Q and compactify to X′(r).

items.name: Harpaz–Wittenberg norm-value approximation conjecture
items.statement: For a number field k, distinct monic irreducibles P_i∈k[t], k_i=k[t]/P_i with a_i=t mod P_i, finite L_i/k_i, b_i∈k_i×, and finite S containing infinite places and the bad places for b_i and L_i/k_i, suppose t_v∈k_v satisfy b_i(t_v−a_i)∈N((L_i⊗_k k_v)×) for v∈S. There should exist t₀∈k arbitrarily close to all t_v such that, for every finite place w of k_i with w(t₀−a_i)>0, either w lies above S or L_i has a degree-one place above w.

items.name: Cover attached to an injective type
items.statement: For finite R̂ and injective λ:R̂→Pic(V_kbar)=Hom(H^ab,kbar×), dualize to a surjection λ̂:H→R(kbar). Over kbar, G/ker λ̂→V is the R-torsor of type λ.

items.name: Real-solubility weak-approximation property
items.statement: A smooth k-variety has property (⋆) if, whenever it has points over every real completion, it has a k-rational point and satisfies weak approximation. Over a number field without real places, the antecedent is vacuous.

items.name: Supersolvability for an outer Galois action
items.statement: A finite group H with continuous outer Γ_k-action is supersolvable if it has a chain 1=H₀⊲H₁⊲…⊲H_m=H, each H_i normal in H and invariant under the outer action, and each H_(i+1)/H_i cyclic.

items.name: Rational-point conjecture for rationally connected varieties
items.statement: The conjectural assertion is that every smooth proper rationally connected variety X over a number field has X(k) dense in X(A_k)^Br(X). The paper proves specified homogeneous-space cases only.

items.name: Quotient of a homogeneous space by a normal subgroup
items.statement: For a connected linear group G over a characteristic-zero field k, a homogeneous G-space V (without a chosen k-point), and a closed normal k-subgroup N⊂G, construct V/N as a homogeneous G/N-space and a smooth surjective G-equivariant quotient map V→V/N whose geometric fibres are N-orbits.

items.name: Determinant-corrected regular embedding
items.statement: For a finite group E, its regular permutation representation together with the inverse determinant character is a faithful embedding E→SL_(|E|+1); apply with E=U and later T(W).

items.name: Homogeneous splitting variety
items.statement: Let N=|U|+1 and V=(SL_N×T_α)/U for the diagonal right action, using U→A on the torsor. It is an SL_N-homogeneous k-variety with geometric stabilizer U¹.

items.name: Geometric stabilizer with outer Galois action
items.statement: For homogeneous V under G and x∈V(kbar), set H_x=Stab_Gbar(x), G_x={(g,σ):g σ(x)=x}⊂G(kbar)⋊Γ_k. The extension by H_x defines Γ_k→Out(H_x).

items.name: Outer-action supersolvability
items.statement: A finite H with outer Γ-action is supersolvable if it has a filtration by normal subgroups, stable under Γ, with cyclic successive quotients. The action condition is part of the definition.

items.name: Picard group of a finite-stabilizer homogeneous space
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for semisimple simply connected G and homogeneous V with finite geometric stabilizer H, Pic(V_kbar)≅Hom(H^ab,kbar×)≅Hom(H^ab,μ∞), equivariantly for Γ_k.

items.name: Finite splitting data for Brauer computation
items.statement: In §3's setting (k of characteristic 0; V a homogeneous space of a semisimple simply connected group with finite geometric stabilizer H; Pic(V_k̄) ≅ Hom(H^ab, k̄^×)): Choose finite Galois L/k containing μ_e, with V(L)≠∅ and outer action on H factoring through G=Gal(L/k); χ:G→(Z/e)× is cyclotomic. The induced H^ab and its character module are G-modules.

items.name: Minimal splitting field of α and χ
items.statement: Take L fixed by ker(α,χ)⊂Γ_k. Then G embeds in A×(Z/e)×, is abelian, L contains μ_e and V(L)≠∅.

items.name: Auxiliary homogeneous space
items.statement: From a defining lift Γ_k→U/Z obtain barα:Γ_k→U/P. Define W=(SL_N×T_barα)/U, with geometric stabilizer P, and the induced SL_N-equivariant morphism π:W→V.

items.name: Order-512 extension and its splitting variety
items.statement: Let ζ:Q→F_2 be the r-coordinate and f(q,q′)=γ(q)ζ(q′). It is a normalized B-valued 2-cocycle. Define E=B×_f Q by (v,q)(w,q′)=(v+q w+f(q,q′),qq′); then 1→B→E→Q→1 has |E|=512. Over k=C((x))((y))((z)), L=k(sqrt x,fourthroot y,sqrt z) has Galois group Q. The augmented regular representation embeds E in SL_513, and V=(SL_513×Spec L)/E is the finite-embedding-problem splitting variety with geometric stabilizer B.

items.name: p-adic discs B(P, r) and the evaluation filtration Ev_n Br X
items.statement: Setting of §§1, 3, 7–9: k is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O_k, uniformiser π, residue field 𝔽 and absolute ramification index e, and e′ = ep/(p−1). X/k is smooth and geometrically irreducible, 𝒳 → Spec O_k is a smooth model of X (not assumed proper) whose special fibre Y is geometrically irreducible, F is the function field of Y and K^h is the fraction field of a Henselisation of O_{𝒳,Y}. For a finite extension k′/k with ramification index e(k′/k), uniformiser π′, r ≥ 1 and P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}), B(P, r) is the set of Q ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}) with the same image as P in 𝒳(O_{k′}/(π′)^r). For A ∈ Br X let |A| : 𝒳(O_{k′}) → Br k′ be evaluation. Then Ev_n Br X = {A : for all finite k′/k and all P ∈ 𝒳(O_{k′}), |A| is constant on B(P, e(k′/k)(n+1))} for n ≥ 0; Ev_{−1} Br X = {A : |A| is constant on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite k′/k}; Ev_{−2} Br X = {A : |A| is zero on 𝒳(O_{k′}) for all finite k′/k}.

items.name: Log-pole residues and the isomorphisms ψ, φ at a blown-up point
items.statement: For a smooth prime divisor D in a smooth variety over a field: 0 → Ω^q → Ω^q(log D) →(ρ) Ω^{q−1}_D → 0, ρ(η + g dlog f) = g|_D. For Y smooth of dimension m over a field L, P₀ ∈ Y(L), the blowup f : Ỹ → Spec O_{Y,P₀} with exceptional Z ≅ P^{m−1}_L: ψ : Ω¹_{Y/L}|_{P₀} ≅ H⁰(Z, O(1)), ψ(dx) = x^{(1)}, and φ : Ω²_{Y/L}|_{P₀} ≅ H⁰(Z, Ω¹_{Z/L}(2)), φ(dx_i ∧ dx_j) = (x_j^{(1)})² d(x_i^{(1)}/x_j^{(1)}).

items.name: The modified adelic Chow group CH_{0,A}(X), completions, and the complex (E)
items.statement: For smooth proper X over a number field k, CH_{0,A}(X) = ∏_{v∈Ω_f} CH_0(X⊗k_v) × ∏_{v∈Ω_∞} CH_0(X⊗k_v)/N_{k̄_v/k_v}(CH_0(X⊗k̄_v)). For an abelian group M, M̂ = lim_n M/nM. The complex (E) is ĈH_0(X) → ĈH_{0,A}(X) → Hom(Br(X), Q/Z), the second map being Σ_v ⟨−,−⟩_v. It is a complex by global reciprocity. Z_{0,A}(X) is the set of families (z_v) whose supports are integral over O_v for almost all v with respect to a model.

items.name: Definition 1.7: properties (E) and (E₁)
items.statement: A smooth proper variety X over a number field k satisfies (E) if (E) is exact. It satisfies (E₁) if the existence of (z_v) ∈ ∏_v Z_0(X⊗k_v) orthogonal to Br(X) with deg(z_v) = 1 for all v implies the existence of a zero-cycle of degree 1 on X. (E) implies (E₁).

items.name: Split varieties, symmetric products and effective reduced cycles over a curve
items.statement: A variety over k is split if it contains a geometrically integral open subset. Sym_{X/k} = ⊔_{d≥1} Sym^d_{X/k} for quasi-projective X. For f : X → C to a smooth proper curve, Z_0^{eff,red}(X) is the set of effective zero-cycles z with f_*z reduced. Over a number field, Z^{eff,red}_{0,A}(X) = Z_{0,A}(X) ∩ ∏_v Z_0^{eff,red}(X⊗k_v). For y ∈ Pic(C), Z^{eff,red,y}_{0,A}(X) consists of families with f_*z_v linearly equivalent to y at finite v, and equivalent up to a norm from k̄_v at infinite v.

items.name: Definition 2.1: the groups Pic₊(C) and Br₊(C)
items.statement: Let C be a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field k of characteristic 0, C⁰ = C ∖ M dense open, and for m ∈ M a nonzero finite étale k(m)-algebra L_m. Pic₊(C) is Div(C⁰) modulo div(f) for those f invertible at every m ∈ M with f(m) ∈ N_{L_m/k(m)}(L_m^*). Br₊(C) ⊆ Br(C⁰) is the set of classes whose residue at each m ∈ M lies in Ker(r_m : H¹(k(m), Q/Z) → H¹(L_m, Q/Z)). There are exact sequences k^* → ⊕_m k(m)^*/N(L_m^*) → Pic₊(C) → Pic(C) → 0 and 0 → Br(C) → Br₊(C) → ⊕_m Ker(r_m) → H³(C, 𝔾_m). In particular Br₊(C)/Br(C) is finite.

items.name: Construction of c₁, v₀ and the divisor c
items.statement: By Theorem 2.5 there is c₁ ∈ Div(C⁰) of class y whose class in Pic₊,A(C) equals that of (f_*z_v). Fix v₀ ∉ S split completely in all L_m. For each m, Lemma 5.2 gives t_m ∈ k(m)^* close to h_v(m) at S ∪ Ω_∞, integral away from S ∪ {v₀}, with divisor supported on places above S or split in L_m. Since deg(y) ≥ deg(M) + 2g + 2, H¹(𝒞, 𝒪(c̃₁ − M̃)) = 0, so H⁰(𝒞, 𝒪(c̃₁)) → H⁰(M̃, 𝒪) is a split surjection of free 𝒪_S-modules. Strong approximation off v₀ in its kernel gives h ∈ H⁰(C, 𝒪(c₁)) with h(m) = t_m, close to h_v at S ∪ Ω_∞, with no pole outside Supp(c̃₁) ∪ 𝒞_{v₀}. Then c = c₁ + div(h).

items.name: Definition 9.4: almost abelian extensions
items.statement: A finite extension L/k is almost abelian if it is abelian, or if for some prime p there is a bijection Spec(L⊗_k k̄) ≅ 𝔽_p under which Gal(k̄/k) acts by affine transformations x ↦ ax + b. Examples 9.5: cubic extensions, and k(c^{1/p})/k.

items.name: The variety W of §9.2.2 and Proposition 9.9
items.statement: W is the fiber over 0 of (A² ∖ {0}) × ∏_i (R_{L_i/k}(A¹) ∖ F_i) → ∏_i R_{k_i/k}(A¹), (λ, μ, x) ↦ (b_i(λ − a_iμ) − N_{L_i/k_i}(x_i))_i, with p : W → P^1 the projection. Proposition 9.9: Conjecture 9.1 holds for all S, (t_v) if and only if ∪_{c∈P^1(k)} W_c(A_k) is dense in W(A_k). Its converse direction uses Theorem 9.17 with B = 0 and Br_vert(W/P^1) = Br(k).

items.name: Geometric rational connectedness
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically integral variety in characteristic zero is rationally connected if two general geometric points can be joined by a rational curve, in the sense of Kollár IV Definition 3.2.2. This is a geometric condition and is independent of extending the algebraically closed ground field.

items.name: Modified local Chow groups
items.statement: CH₀,A(X)=∏_{v finite}CH₀(X_kv) × ∏_{v infinite}coker(N:CH₀(X_kbarv)→CH₀(X_kv)). Complex factors vanish; real factors are quotients by norm.

items.name: Completion of the zero-cycle complex
items.statement: For an abelian group M let M̂=lim_{n by divisibility} M/nM. Complete CH₀(X) and CH₀,A(X); their Brauer pairings define the complex CH₀(X)^∧→CH₀,A(X)^∧→Hom(Br(X),Q/Z).

items.name: Exactness property (E)
items.statement: For a smooth proper irreducible k-variety over a number field, property (E) is exactness at the middle of CH₀(X)^∧→CH₀,A(X)^∧→Hom(Br(X),Q/Z). It is not a claim of surjectivity onto the last group.

items.name: Prime-to-p coset diagram
items.statement: With E₀ the inverse image of Γ_p, the exact rows 1→H_p→E_p→Γ_p→1 and 1→H→E₀→Γ_p→1 give an identification of finite coset sets H/H_p≅E₀/E_p of cardinal prime to p.

items.name: Good property of homogeneous spaces
items.statement: For connected linear homogeneous spaces, the paper calls P good if it is stable-birationally invariant, descends along a morphism with a section, and ascends a surjection whose fibres are homogeneous under semisimple simply connected groups with geometric stabilizers extensions of semisimple groups by connected unipotent groups.

items.name: Stable fibration form of the zero-cycle property
items.statement: For smooth proper irreducible X/k, E⁺(X) means: every smooth proper irreducible Z dominating X satisfies E if its geometric generic fibre is rationally connected and there is a dense open X₀ such that for every finite k′/k and x∈X₀(k′), the fibre Z_x satisfies (⋆) over k′.

items.name: Middle cohomology of the zero-cycle complex
items.statement: For smooth proper irreducible X/k let h_X=ker(CH₀,A(X)^∧→Hom(Br(X),Q/Z))/im(CH₀(X)^∧). Proper morphisms induce h_Y→h_X by cycle pushforward and Brauer pullback; birational morphisms induce isomorphisms.

items.name: Reinterpreting a finite-extension variety over k
items.statement: For finite ℓ/k, a smooth proper geometrically integral ℓ-variety Y is a smooth proper irreducible k-variety through Spec ℓ→Spec k. Its k-adic cycle complex agrees with the ℓ-adic one after grouping places above v, with the real/complex norm factors respected. E and the finite-extension fibre tests for E⁺ transfer through this dictionary.

items.name: Zero-cycle image condition for Brauer–Manin points
items.statement: For smooth proper geometrically integral Y over a number field, HW16 Condition 8.1 says that the image of Y(A_k)^Br(Y) in CH₀,A(Y)^∧ is contained in the image of CH₀(Y)^∧.

items.name: Uncompleted zero-cycle conjecture in the rationally connected case
items.statement: For every smooth proper rationally connected X over a number field, the uncompleted complex (1.1) from global zero-cycles to the modified local product to Hom(Br(X),Q/Z) is conjectured exact. Rappel 1.3 identifies this with E for this class.

items.name: DLA good property on birational homogeneous-space models
items.statement: Over a characteristic-zero field K, a property P on smooth geometrically integral K-varieties birational to connected linear homogeneous spaces is DLA-good if it is invariant under stable birational equivalence, descends along morphisms with a section, and ascends every surjective morphism all of whose fibres over w are homogeneous under G_w=G_w^ssu with (G_w)^ss simply connected and geometric stabilizer H_w=H_w^ssu. Here G^red=G°/R_u(G°), G^ss=[G^red,G^red], G^tor=G^red/G^ss and G^ssu=ker(G°→G^tor).

items.name: Resolution above the field of two elements
items.statement: The hypothesis has TWO clauses: every proper integral F_2-variety admits a proper birational morphism from a smooth F_2-variety; and every smooth affine F_2-variety admits an open immersion into a smooth projective F_2-variety whose complement is a simple normal crossings divisor. This is an assumption, not a theorem asserted here.

items.name: Torsion Tate coefficient complex
items.statement: For n>0, Z/n(i)=μ_n^{⊗i} if char F does not divide n. If char F=p and n=mp^r with p∤m, use μ_m^{⊗i}⊕W_rΩ^i_log[-i] on the étale site. Hence H^j(F,Z/n(i)) has wild summand H^{j-i}(F,W_rΩ^i_log). The paper uses n=2 and i>=0.

items.name: Shifted Kato cohomology convention
items.statement: For i>=0 set H^{i+1}(F)=H^{i+1}(F,Z/2(i)); in characteristic two this is H^1(F,Ω^i_log), not ordinary H^{i+1}(G_F,μ_2^{⊗i}).

items.name: Restriction in Kato cohomology
items.statement: For a field extension E/F, pullback of the coefficient complexes induces res_E/F:H^{i+1}(F)→H^{i+1}(E), compatible with identity and composition.

items.name: Discrete valuation residue
items.statement: In the coefficient/valuation regimes used in Facts 2.1–2.3, a discrete valuation w of F has a boundary ∂_w:H^{i+1}(F)→H^i(Fw), factoring through restriction to the w-henselization. In mixed residue characteristic two the required hypotheses must be supplied separately; no unrestricted residue map is inferred.

items.name: Fields obtained from global constant places
items.statement: For a relatively algebraically closed global subfield k_1⊂K and a place v of k_1, take k_{1v} to be its henselization at finite v, its real closure at real v, and its algebraic closure at complex v inside the completion. Let K_v=Kk_{1v}, embedded in the corresponding function field over the completion. Keep henselian and completed fields distinct.

items.name: Arithmetic Bloch–Ogus complex
items.statement: For the excellent normal integral d-dimensional schemes in Facts 2.2–2.3, form the homological complex with degree a term ⊕_{x:dim closure{x}=a}H^{a+1}(κ(x)); its top term is H^{d+1}(κ(X)) and top differential is the sum of codimension-one residues. The residue differentials satisfy d²=0.

items.name: The groups H^i(L, Z/nZ(j)) and H^i(L, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j))
items.statement: For a field L and n > 0: H^i(L, Z/nZ(j)) = H^i(L, μ_n^{⊗j}) if char L = 0, and H^i(L, μ_m^{⊗j}) ⊕ H^{i−j}(L, W_rΩ^j_{L,log}) if char L = p > 0, n = m p^r, p ∤ m. Then Br(L)[n] = H²(L, Z/nZ(1)). H^i(L, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) = colim_n H^i(L, Z/ℓ^nZ(j)) along Z/ℓ^n(j) ↪ Z/ℓ^{n+1}(j).

items.name: Kato complexes C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ) (Kato; Bloch–Ogus)
items.statement: For X excellent (a variety over a field) and n ≥ 1, C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ): ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_a} H^{r+a}(k(x), Z/nZ(s+a)) →∂ ⊕_{x∈X_{a−1}} H^{r+a−1}(k(x), Z/nZ(s+a−1)) → ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_0} H^r(k(x), Z/nZ(s)), with X_a the points of dimension a in degree a. Kato defines it via Galois cohomology of discrete valuation fields under condition (∗) (if r = s+1 and p | n then [k(x) : k(x)^p] ≤ s for x ∈ X_0 of characteristic p). For X of finite type over a field L with n invertible it is Bloch–Ogus's E¹_{·,−r}(X, Z/nZ(−s)) of the niveau spectral sequence for étale homology H_a(X, Z/nZ(b)) = H^{−a}(X, Rf^!Z/nZ(−b)) (4.1)–(4.2), with ∂_{y,x} given by Gysin residues at smooth points and by normalization and corestriction (4.3)–(4.4) otherwise; the two definitions agree up to well-defined signs [JSS14]. Special cases: C^{2,1} (global/local fields), C^{1,0} (finite fields), C^{0,0}.

items.name: Quadratic Pfister form in characteristic two
items.statement: For char F=2 and a_i,…,a_0∈F×, q_a is the tensor product of the bilinear factors ⟨1,−a_j⟩, j=i,…,1, with the quadratic binary form x²+xy+a_0y². It is a nonsingular quadratic form of dimension 2^{i+1}; replacing the final factor by a diagonal form is wrong.

items.name: Cohomological symbol of a Pfister form
items.statement: An (i+1)-fold quadratic Pfister form q_a has its canonical symbol invariant e(q_a)∈H^{i+1}(F,Z/2(i)): the usual mod-two Kummer symbol away from characteristic two and the characteristic-two quadratic/logarithmic invariant in EKM§16. Its normalization uses q=x²+xy+a_0y² in characteristic two.

items.name: Restricted monomial system
items.statement: A finite set M of distinct exponent vectors in (Fin 2 →₀ ℕ) specifies monomials in MvPolynomial (Fin 2) F over a field F. Put D=|M|, p=Σ_(i,j)∈M(i+j), q=Σ_(i,j)∈M j. For any finite point-index type S and z:S→F², A_(s,m)=z_s^m is an S-by-M evaluation matrix. The source uses D>0; the coefficient/evaluation API also permits M=∅.

items.name: Scaled derivative bound
items.statement: For N>0, k∈ℕ, a nonempty compact interval I⊂[0,N], an open U containing I and f:ℝ→ℝ of class C^k on U, let ||f||_(N,k;I)=max_{0≤r≤k, x∈I} N^(r−1)|iteratedDeriv r f x|/r!. Exponents here are real/integer, not truncated natural subtraction. This specifies the open-neighbourhood specialization used for the graph applications; it does not identify arbitrary closed-set within-derivatives with ordinary endpoint derivatives.

items.name: Monomials avoiding the leading term
items.statement: For a degree-d plane polynomial F and integer δ≥2d, select monomials of degrees d through δ not divisible by the degree-d term of largest Y-degree in F. Then D=d(δ−d+1), p=d(δ(δ+1)−d(d−1))/2.

items.name: Logarithmic potential, energy, capacity and the equilibrium measure
items.statement: For Σ ⊂ ℂ compact and µ a Borel measure on Σ, the potential function is U^µ(z) = ∫_Σ −log|z − w| dµ(w) and the energy is I(µ) = ∫_Σ U^µ dµ ∈ ℝ ∪ {∞}. The capacity of Σ is κ_Σ = sup_µ e^{−I(µ)} over probability measures supported in Σ. If κ_Σ > 0 the supremum is attained by a unique probability measure of minimal energy, the unweighted equilibrium measure µ_Σ of Σ.

items.name: Hölder measures
items.statement: A Borel measure µ on ℝ is η-Hölder for η > 0 if there is C > 0 with µ([x, y]) ≤ C(y − x)^η for all x < y; µ is Hölder if it is η-Hölder for some η > 0.

items.name: Compact finite unions of intervals
items.statement: A compact Σ ⊂ ℝ is a compact finite union of intervals if it is nonempty, has finitely many connected components and has no isolated points.

items.name: The weight w_µ and the n-norm
items.statement: For a Hölder measure µ supported in a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, the weight is w_µ(z) = exp(U^µ(z)) ∈ ℝ_{>0} ∪ {∞}. For a complex polynomial P and n ≥ 0, the n-norm of P with respect to (µ, Σ) is ‖w_µ^n P‖_Σ = max_{x ∈ Σ} (w_µ(x)^n |P(x)|).

items.name: The approximating polynomial of a measure
items.statement: For Σ ⊂ ℝ compact, µ a Hölder probability measure on Σ and n ≥ 1, let α_i be the least α ∈ Σ with µ((−∞, α]) = i/n for 0 ≤ i ≤ n, and set P_{n,µ}(z) = ∏_{i=1}^n (z − α_i). Then −n^{-1} ≤ (µ_{P_{n,µ}} − µ)((−∞, x]) ≤ 0 for all x, so |(µ_{P_{n,µ}} − µ)(I)| ≤ n^{-1} for every closed interval I.

items.name: Pruned polynomials
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and P a real monic squarefree polynomial with root set S, suppose there is a subset S̃ ⊆ S ∩ Σ of cardinality n such that for every connected component I of Σ meeting S, the set I ∩ S̃ contains neither the least nor the greatest element of I ∩ S. Then ∏_{α ∈ S̃}(z − α) is a degree n pruned polynomial of P.

items.name: Complementary polynomials
items.statement: Given Σ, κ, C₁, D as above, a real monic P of degree n and r ≥ 2, take T from Lemma 4.5 and set Q₀(x) = ∏_{j=0}^{D−1}(T(x) − ((2j+1)/(4DC₁))κ^r). With d = rD − r, choose ε_d, …, ε₁ ≥ 0 minimal in turn so that (Q₀ + ε_dT_d + ⋯ + ε_iT_i)·P has an even coefficient in degree d + n + 1 − (d − i + 1), and put Q = Q₀ + ε_dT_d + ⋯ + ε₁T₁ + N with N ≥ 0 minimal so that |Q(α)| ≥ n^{-1}C₂^{-1}κ^{Dr} at every root α of P, where C₂ = 8(4DC₁)^D. This Q is the complementary polynomial to P of degree Dr, and every coefficient of PQ in the relevant range is an even integer.

items.name: The measure ν_[a,b] and its potential
items.statement: For b > a > 0 let ν_{[a,b]} be the measure on [a,b] with dν_{[a,b]}(t) = √(ab) dt/(πt√((b−t)(t−a))). It is a 1/2-Hölder probability measure, U^{ν_{[a,b]}}(z) + log|z| − log((a + 2√(ab) + b)/(b−a)) vanishes for z ∈ [a,b] and is ≤ 0 otherwise, and U^{ν_{[a,b]}}(0) = log((a + 2√(ab) + b)/(4ab)).

items.name: Smoothing by convolution and its effect on potentials
items.statement: For ε ∈ (0, 1/2) put ν_ε = ν_{[ε², ε]}. For a Borel measure µ on a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, the convolution µ * ν_ε is 1/2-Hölder with support in {x : [x − ε, x − ε²] ∩ Σ ≠ ∅}, and U^{µ*ν_ε}(z) − U^µ(z) ≤ log((ε² + 2ε^{3/2} + ε)/(ε − ε²)) ≤ Cε^{1/2} uniformly in z, ε and µ. If µ * ν_ε is supported in Σ for all small ε, then µ * ν_ε → µ weak* as ε → 0.

items.name: Sweetened measures
items.statement: Let Σ ⊂ ℝ be compact of capacity κ > 1, Σ′ ⊇ Σ compact, µ a probability measure and ν a measure on Σ′ with γ = 1 − ν(Σ′) ∈ [0,1]. Let µ_Σ be the unweighted equilibrium measure of Σ and B = sup_{U^µ(z)<∞}(U^{ν+γµ_Σ}(z) − U^µ(z)), assumed finite; then B ≥ 0. The sweetened measure of ν with respect to Σ and µ is sw(ν) = (β + γ − βγ)µ_Σ + (1−β)ν, where β ∈ [0,1) satisfies β/(1−β) = B/log κ; β + γ − βγ is the measure of sweetener. It satisfies U^{sw(ν)}(z) ≤ (1−β)U^µ(z) for all z.

items.name: The optimisation constants λ(Σ, F) and λ_Smyth(Σ, F)
items.statement: Let Σ ⊆ ℝ be closed with at most countably many components and capacity > 1, and F : Σ → ℝ continuous with F(x_i)/log|x_i| → +∞ along any sequence with |x_i| → ∞ when Σ is unbounded. Enumerating the algebraic integers α_i all of whose conjugates lie in Σ, with degrees n_i and minimal polynomials P_i, set λ(Σ,F) = liminf_i ∫_Σ F dµ_{P_i}. Let λ_Smyth(Σ,F) be the least upper bound of the λ for which there are nonzero integer polynomials Q₁,…,Q_N and positive a₁,…,a_N with F(x) ≥ λ + Σ_i a_i log|Q_i(x)| for all x ∈ Σ.

items.name: Serre's measure and the proof of Theorem 1.1
items.statement: Take a = 0.087353, b = 4.411076, γ = 0.215485 and µ = γν_{[a,b]} + (1−γ)µ_{[a,b]}, where µ_{[a,b]} is the unweighted equilibrium measure of [a,b]. Then U^µ(z) + γ log|z| equals a constant C ≈ −1.3·10^{−7} on [a,b] and is at most C elsewhere, ∫log|x| dµ(x) ≈ 1.5·10^{−6} is nonnegative, so Proposition 5.15 applies with Q₁(z) = z; and ∫x dµ(x) = γ√(ab) + (1−γ)(a+b)/2 ∈ (1.898303, 1.898304). Applying Theorem 1.5 to µ proves Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Upper semicontinuity of log|Q| and Serre's implication
items.statement: For a nonzero integer polynomial Q the function log|Q| is upper semicontinuous on a compact Σ ⊂ ℝ, so for a weak*-convergent sequence of counting measures µ_{R_k} → µ one has ∫_Σ log|Q| dµ ≥ limsup_k ∫_Σ log|Q| dµ_{R_k} = limsup_k log|res(R_k,Q)|/deg R_k ≥ 0.

items.name: Galois cochain DGA comparison
items.statement: For a profinite Γ and finite coefficient ring with continuous action, construct all-degree continuous inhomogeneous cochains with associative cup and Leibniz, and compare its H¹,H² and cup to the canonical continuous theory.

items.name: Elementary transvections
items.statement: For i<j, e_ij(t)=1+t E_ij lies in U; e_ij=e_ij(1). Entries strictly above the diagonal give a unique ordered product expansion.

items.name: Center and superdiagonal quotient
items.statement: For n≥2, Z=U^(n-1)=<e_0n>≅F_p is the center, and A=U/U¹≅F_p^n via adjacent entries.

items.name: Outer exponent
items.statement: For finite H with exponent d, its outer exponent e is the least divisor of d such that the units (Z/d)× acting on conjugacy classes by powering factor through (Z/e)×.

items.name: Conjugacy-power test pairing
items.statement: If σ[u]=[u^χ(σ)] in H/conj, then ubar in H^ab is χ(σ)-eigen; viewed in Hom(character(H^ab),μ∞_trivial), it is σ-fixed and pairs σ*β∈H¹(Z,character(H^ab)) with μ∞ via 1↦σ.

items.name: Bogomolov multiplier
items.statement: For a finite group H, B_0(H)=ker(H²(H,Q/Z)→∏_A H²(A,Q/Z)), A ranging over abelian subgroups; equivalently test bicyclic subgroups. Coefficients have trivial action.

items.name: Abelianized stabilizer module
items.statement: B=U¹/U³=(U¹)^ab is an F_p-space with basis e_ij for j-i=2 or 3, dimension 2n-3, and A acts by conjugation.

items.name: Cyclically trivial first cohomology
items.statement: Sha¹_cyc(G,M)=ker(H¹(G,M)→∏_C H¹(C,M)), over all cyclic subgroups C of finite G.

items.name: Matrix support ideals
items.statement: N_r is the additive group of upper triangular matrices with M_ij=0 for j-i<r; N_r N_s⊂N_(r+s), N_r=0 for r>n, and M∈U^r iff M-1∈N_(r+1).

items.name: Boundary submodule B0
items.statement: B_0⊂B is spanned by e_02,e_03,e_(n-3),n,e_(n-2),n. It is A-stable, has dimension four for n>3 and dimension three for n=3, when B_0=B. This B_0 is not the Bogomolov multiplier.

items.name: Reversal inverse-transpose involution
items.statement: Let P be the anti-diagonal permutation matrix. τ(M)=(P M^-1 P^-1)^t is an involutive automorphism of U, sending e_ij to e_(n-j),(n-i)^-1 and inducing compatible maps on A and U¹/conjugacy classes.

items.name: Two-boundary subgroup
items.statement: For n≥3 and 1≤r,s≤n-2, P_(r,s) is generated by e_i,n (0≤i≤r) and e_0,j (n-s≤j≤n); the shared e_0n occurs once.

items.name: Torsor of splittings of a module sequence
items.statement: Assume C is finite (as in this paper’s applications). For 0→A→B→C→0 of discrete Γ-modules split as abelian groups, the sections form a Hom(C,A)-torsor with conjugation action. For a section s, γ(g)=g s g^-1-s represents its class.

items.name: Twisted local boundary sequence
items.statement: Given a continuous lift tildeα:Γ_K→U/Z of α:Γ_K→U/P, conjugation gives Γ-actions on P and P/Z and an exact sequence 0→Z→P→P/Z→0 of modules; it is split as abelian groups.

items.name: Explicit boundary retractions
items.statement: Write W=F_p^(n+1), row u∈W*, column v∈W. If u_0 v_n=1, ρ_(u,v)(Q)=u(Q-1)v gives a retraction P→Z; every group retraction arises this way. With u_0,v_n fixed, equality is exactly the indicated row/column truncation equivalence.

items.name: Row and column coordinate filtrations
items.statement: W^m consists of columns supported at indices 0,…,m, and W*_m of rows supported at n-m,…,n. They are U-stable for the corresponding actions and control the annihilator formulas for ρ.

items.name: Stabilizer of a boundary retraction
items.statement: For an equivariant retraction ρ_(u,v), let S⊂U stabilize it under conjugation. Then P⊂S, tildeα lands in S/Z, and M∈S iff u(M-1)∈W*_(n-r-1) and (M-1)v∈W^(n-s-1).

items.name: Central commutator map
items.statement: For n=5 and Q lifting e_14+b, U³=<e_04,e_15,e_05> is central in U¹. The map Θ_Q:B→U³, Mbar↦M^-1QMQ^-1, is a homomorphism.

items.name: Galois coefficient system with compositions
items.statement: For 0≤i<j≤n take discrete Γ_k-modules M_ij and equivariant biadditive M_ij⊗M_jl→M_il satisfying associativity. Defining systems use the twisted cups and target H²(k,M_0n).

items.name: Hom coefficient system
items.statement: For a finite commutative ring R and finite Galois R-modules N_i, let M_ij=Hom_R(N_j,N_i), with action g·f=g_Ni f g_Nj^-1 and multiplication composition.

items.name: Filtered automorphism group
items.statement: For W=⊕_(i=0)^n N_i with W_m=⊕_(i≤m)N_i, T(W) is the finite group of R-linear automorphisms preserving each W_m, with diagonal map ρ:T→∏Aut_R(N_i).

items.name: Unipotent filtered kernels
items.statement: U(W)=kerρ is finite nilpotent. U¹(W) acts identically on W_i/W_(i-2), i=1,…,n; it is normal in T. A(W)=T/U¹ fits the split extension with kernel ⊕Hom(N_(i+1),N_i) and diagonal quotient.

items.name: Character and cocycle lift
items.statement: The actions on N_i define χ:Γ_k→∏Aut_R(N_i). Chosen representatives of α_i∈H¹(k,M_i,i+1) give a continuous α:Γ_k→A(W); changing them by coboundaries conjugates α by the additive kernel.

items.name: Twisted corner kernel
items.statement: Z(W)=Hom_R(N_n,N_0) embeds in U¹ via the corner transvections. It is abelian, normal in T and central in U, but in general not central in T.

items.name: Twisted extension class
items.statement: The extension 1→Z(W)→T(W)→T(W)/Z(W)→1 has class u∈H²(T/Z,Z) with conjugation coefficients; pullback along a lift of α recovers precisely the prescribed Γ_k-action on M_0n.

items.name: Boundary subgroup with twisted coefficients
items.statement: For r+s=n-1, P is the internal sum in End(W) of Hom(N_n,N_i), 0≤i≤r, and Hom(N_j,N_0), n-s≤j≤n. Their intersection is Z=Hom(N_n,N_0); count it once.

items.name: Abelian kernel for the Z/8 example
items.statement: In U_(Z/8)=UT_4(Z/8), let P=<e_02,e_03,e_12,e_13>≅(Z/8)^4 and U¹=<e_02,e_03,e_13>. Then C=U/P≅(Z/8)^2 with basis e_01,e_23, and C acts on P by conjugation.

items.name: Dual module sequence and boundary
items.statement: Dualizing 0→<e_03>→U¹→<e_02,e_13>→0 gives 0→μ_8²→character(U¹)→μ_8→0. Over Q, the boundary sends -1 to ([16q^4],[p^4]) in (Q×/Q×8)^2.

items.name: Invariant Sha coordinates over L
items.statement: Over L of item126, write W=Sha¹(L,μ_8)⊂L×/L×8 multiplicatively and s=e_01,t=e_23∈C. Sha¹(L,character U¹)^C consists of triples (a02,a03,a13)∈W³ with s(a13)=a03 a13, s(a02)=a02, s(a03)=a03, t(a02)=a02 a03^-1, t(a03)=a03, t(a13)=a13. Sha¹(L,character P)^C consists of quadruples (a02,a03,a12,a13)∈W⁴ with s(a1j)=a0j a1j and s(a0j)=a0j for j=2,3, and t(ai2)=ai2 ai3^-1 and t(ai3)=ai3 for i=0,1. The restriction map deletes coordinate12.

items.name: Choice of the middle character
items.statement: Choose 0≠γ in the preceding kernel. Exactness of 0→U¹→P→Z/8→0 supplies χ_12∈H¹(Q,Z/8) with ∂χ_12=γ; γ is zero over every completion and nonzero globally.

items.name: Five-dimensional obstruction module
items.statement: Let B=F_2 a⊕F_2 b⊕F_2 c⊕F_2 d⊕F_2 e. On Q=C2(s)×C4(t)×C2(r) let r act trivially, s=1+N_s,t=1+N_t with N_s(b)=d+e,N_s(c)=e,N_t(a)=d,N_t(b)=d+e and all other basis images zero. These endomorphisms have square zero and zero pairwise products, so define the claimed action.

items.name: Auxiliary cocycle on the quartic quotient
items.statement: On the Q-module B of item144 define γ(s)=a,γ(t)=b+c,γ(r)=0 and extend by γ(uv)=γ(u)+uγ(v). This is well-defined: N_s(b+c)=d=N_t(a), the s-norm of a is zero and the t-fourth norm of b+c is zero. Explicitly γ(s^i t^j r^l)=ia+s^i Σ_(h<j)t^h(b+c). Its b-coordinate is j mod2 and γ(t²)=d+e.

items.name: Universal solvability over a base field
items.statement: An abelian-kernel extension has a positive embedding-problem answer over F if every continuous Γ_K→H lifts for every field extension K/F.

items.name: Negligible cohomology
items.statement: For finite H, an H-module A and d≥0, H^d_neg,F(H,A) is the subgroup of classes α such that ρ*α=0 for every extension K/F and continuous ρ:Γ_K→H, using A with its pulled-back discrete action.

items.name: Generic Galois extension
items.statement: A faithful finite-dimensional representation V of finite H over F makes L=F(V) a Galois extension of K=F(V)^H with group H, inducing a surjective continuous Γ_K→H after an embedding L⊂K^sep.

items.name: Inverse Tate twist with finite coefficients
items.statement: Given n≥1, nA=0 and a field containing μ_n, define A(−1)=Hom_Z(μ_n,A), with H acting through A and trivially on μ_n.

items.name: Tensor–Kummer isomorphism ι
items.statement: For finite H-module A killed by n, H-Galois L/K, and μ_n⊂K, ι:A(−1)⊗_Z L×≅H¹(L,A), obtained from Kummer and the cup/evaluation pairing, is H-equivariant.

items.name: The gamma map
items.statement: For finite H-module A killed by n and H-Galois L/K with μ_ne⊂K, e(H)|e, define γ:(A(−1)⊗L×)^H→H²(H,A) as tg∘ι.

items.name: The beta map
items.statement: Under §3 hypotheses, β:A(−1)^H⊗(L×/μ_e)^H→(A(−1)⊗L×)^H sends a⊗fμ_e to a⊗f; it is independent of representatives because μ_e consists of nth powers in L×.

items.name: The finite étale algebra and its extension group
items.statement: For the same f, M=L[t]/(t^n−f) is finite étale over L. Choose c_h∈μ_ne with c_h^n=h(f)/f, extend h by t↦c_h t, and let G be all ζh̃. Then 1→μ_n→G→H→1 is central and M/K is a G-Galois algebra.

items.name: The character of the Kummer algebra
items.statement: For the above G-action on M, χ(g)=g(t)/t lies in μ_ne and is a homomorphism restricting to id on μ_n; χ(g)^n=∂₁(fμ_e)(g mod μ_n).

items.name: Cup–corestriction generators
items.statement: For H′≤H define φ_H′:A^H′⊗H²(H′,Z)→H²(H,A), a⊗c↦cor_H′^H(a∪c).

items.name: The generated subgroup
items.statement: Write barH²(H,A) for the subgroup of H²(H,A) generated by the images of all φ_H′, H′≤H; this is not the whole ambient cohomology by definition.

items.name: Divisors of affine representation space
items.statement: For V an affine space over F, Div(V) is the free abelian group on codimension-one points, with its induced H-action when H acts linearly on V.

items.name: Kummer extension class
items.statement: For m,n≥1 with μ_mn⊂F, a Kummer class is the central extension class of 0→Z/n→Z/mn→Z/m→0, with the last map reduction and the first multiplication by m.

items.name: Integral cyclic carry cocycle
items.statement: For m≥1 and a,c∈C_m represented in {0,…,m−1}, κ_m(a,c)=floor((a+c)/m)∈Z. It is normalized and satisfies κ(a,c)+κ(a+c mod m,e)=κ(c,e)+κ(a,c+e mod m).

items.name: Elman–Lam u-invariant
items.statement: For characteristic-zero K, u(K) is the supremum in N∪{∞} of dimensions of anisotropic forms whose signatures vanish at every field ordering. When K has no ordering, the signature condition is vacuous. Keep this distinct from the unrestricted anisotropic-dimension invariant of formally real fields.

items.name: C_i field
items.statement: K is C_i when every homogeneous polynomial of degree d≥1 in more than d^i variables over K has a nontrivial zero.

items.name: Harrison compactness descent of a Brauer class
items.statement: For α∈Br(K)[2] trivial over every real closure and trdeg_R K=2, choose a finitely generated K0⊂K carrying α and a transcendence basis of K/R; then K is the directed union of finite Ki/K0. The closed compact sets of orderings where α_i remains nonzero have empty inverse limit, hence some is empty. This reduces item94 to a real-surface function field.

items.name: Lang's C_i conjecture over R (statement only)
items.statement: The function field of an integral variety X of dimension i over R with X(R) = ∅ is C_i. Not proved; Theorem 0.10 is the case i = 2 for quadratic forms (d = 2).

items.name: Pfister's u-invariant conjecture (statement only)
items.statement: If K/R has transcendence degree i, then the Elman–Lam invariant satisfies u(K) ≤ 2^i. Not proved; Theorem 0.12 is the case i = 2.
